title: Spin-induced Multipartite Steady-state Entanglement Of Motional Modes In Hexagonal Boron Nitride Membranes
authors: Nahid Yazdi, Vahid Salari, Roohollah Ghobadi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we focus on a scheme in which three high-quality-factor mechanical modes of a hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) membrane monolayer are coupled to a common optically addressable spin defect present in the membrane via magnetic field interaction. We show that this coupling induces an effective phonon-phonon interaction in the dispersive regime and under appropriate magnetic field and microwave modulation. We derive the Langevin-Heisenberg equations of motion for vibrational modes to analyze optimal parameter regimes for reaching a physically stable system. We also investigate the effect of coupling strength on purity and entanglement. Our results demonstrate that bipartite and genuinely tripartite steady-state entanglement between different vibrational modes of hBN may be achieved in a broad spectrum of experimental parameters. This study has the potential to enable scalability to be implemented for the generation of two-dimensional continuous-variable cluster states for universal quantum computation.
tldr: This paper proposes a scheme to generate multipartite steady-state entanglement between mechanical modes of a hexagonal boron nitride membrane via coupling to an optically addressable spin defect.
motivation: Generating multipartite entanglement in solid-state systems is crucial for quantum information processing and quantum networks.
method: The authors model three mechanical modes of an hBN membrane coupled to a spin defect via magnetic field, derive Langevin-Heisenberg equations, and analyze parameter regimes for stability and entanglement.
result: Bipartite and genuinely tripartite steady-state entanglement between vibrational modes can be achieved over a broad range of experimental parameters.
conclusion: This scheme could enable scalable generation of two-dimensional continuous-variable cluster states for universal quantum computation.

title: Phonon Heat Transport With Squeezing-based Symmetry Breaking
authors: Yan Cao, Cheng Yang, Xintong Gu, Shenzhu Wang, Jiteng Sheng, Haibin Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The controllability of phonon thermal transport is fundamental for numerous technologies, from cooling high-performance chips to managing heat in quantum computing. Despite extensive efforts, on-demand, real-time control of phonon heat flow remains elusive, being fundamentally constrained by the temperature gradient. Here we achieve this long-sought phonon heat transport by introducing a novel mechanism using quantum squeezing in a cavity optomechanical system. We find that phonon squeezing of near-ground-state mechanical resonators via an optomechanically induced parametric process breaks the continuous U(1) rotation symmetry in phase space, and consequently the symmetry in the heat current structure. We reveal that heat flow under a constant temperature gradient can be deterministically amplified, reduced, or even reversed, a capability previously unattainable. With phonon squeezing, we achieve over twentyfold amplification of heat flow and reversal within 30 milliseconds. Importantly, quantum discord analysis reveals a direct connection between heat flow reversal and quantum correlation. Our results establish quantum squeezing as a versatile platform for on-demand phononic thermal control, opening avenues for active heat management in quantum devices and thermal logic circuits.
tldr: This paper demonstrates on-demand control of phonon heat transport using quantum squeezing in a cavity optomechanical system, achieving amplification, reduction, and reversal of heat flow under a constant temperature gradient.
motivation: Real-time control of phonon heat flow is crucial for thermal management in quantum devices and computing, but has been fundamentally limited by the temperature gradient.
method: The authors introduce quantum squeezing via an optomechanically induced parametric process to break the U(1) rotation symmetry in phase space, enabling control over heat current symmetry.
result: They achieve over twentyfold amplification of heat flow and reversal within 30 milliseconds, with quantum discord analysis linking heat flow reversal to quantum correlations.
conclusion: Quantum squeezing provides a versatile platform for on-demand phononic thermal control, opening avenues for active heat management in quantum devices and thermal logic circuits.

title: Theory Of Approximate Quantum Error Correction And The Error-set Model
authors: Dor Elimelech, Victor V. Albert, Alexander Barg
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a theory of approximate quantum error correction (QEC) based on the error-set model, complemented by general methods for code construction. Exact QEC has a powerful error-set structure: by the Knill-Laflamme conditions, a code correcting a given error set automatically protects against every channel whose Kraus operators lie in their linear span. This linearity gives rise to code distance, the equivalence between erasures and general errors, and a theory of asymptotically good codes. A longstanding view has been that these features do not extend to AQEC, leaving the theory essentially channel-by-channel. We show instead that, although full Knill--Laflamme linearity fails, a restricted form survives and suffices to extend all three structural features to the approximate setting. Specifically, a common error-set criterion governs families of channels whose Kraus operators are linear combinations of a given error set and whose coefficient matrices satisfy a spectral constraint. Using the B\'eny-Oreshkov worst-case and Petz average-case frameworks, we derive uniform fidelity guarantees for these families in terms of two new code parameters--the , controlling worst-case performance, and the , characterizing the average-case performance of Petz recovery. To demonstrate the scope of this model, we develop partition-based constructions across diverse quantum systems and geometries, placing exact and approximate correction on equal footing. These constructions lead to a metric--error alignment hierarchy for Hilbert spaces, metrics, and error families, which in turn characterizes the resulting recovery guarantees. They yield the first known asymptotically good code families for fermionic systems, one-dimensional Rydberg-blockaded systems, and deletion errors, and extend to other physical platforms.
tldr: Develops a theory of approximate quantum error correction that extends the structural features of exact QEC to the approximate setting.
motivation: Exact QEC has powerful structural features (linearity, code distance, asymptotically good codes) that were thought not to extend to approximate QEC, leaving it channel-by-channel.
method: Introduces the error-set model with two new code parameters (worst-case and average-case) and uses Bény-Oreshkov and Petz recovery frameworks to derive uniform fidelity guarantees.
result: Shows that a restricted form of Knill-Laflamme linearity survives, enabling code distance, erasure-equivalence, and asymptotically good code constructions for fermionic, Rydberg-blockaded, and deletion-error systems.
conclusion: Places exact and approximate QEC on equal footing, providing a unified framework and new code families for various physical platforms.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theory of approximate quantum error correction (AQEC) based on an error-set model, extending structural features previously thought exclusive to exact QEC. The authors show that while the full Knill-Laflamme linearity fails for AQEC, a restricted form survives, governed by a spectral constraint on coefficient matrices. This allows them to extend three key features—code distance, equivalence between erasures and general errors, and asymptotically good code constructions—to the approximate setting. They introduce two new code parameters: the environment-leakage distance for worst-case performance and the Knill-Laflamme Hellinger distance for average-case performance under Petz recovery. Using these, they derive uniform fidelity guarantees for families of channels whose Kraus operators lie in the linear span of a given error set. The paper also presents partition-based constructions across diverse quantum systems, leading to a metric-error alignment hierarchy that characterizes recovery guarantees. These constructions yield the first known asymptotically good code families for fermionic systems, one-dimensional Rydberg-blockaded systems, and deletion errors.

The analysis is largely theoretical, with proofs of theorems and lemmas, but also includes explicit constructions for specific physical systems.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper's main results are theoretical, establishing uniform fidelity guarantees for families of channels. For worst-case performance, the environment-leakage distance d_env controls the fidelity: for any channel in the family, the worst-case fidelity is at least 1 - O(ε^{d_env}) for small ε. For average-case Petz recovery, the Knill-Laflamme Hellinger distance d_KLH gives a fidelity lower bound of 1 - O(ε^{d_KLH}). These parameters are shown to be achievable via partition-based constructions. The paper also demonstrates that for fermionic systems, the code rate can approach the noiseless capacity, and for deletion errors, the codes achieve a rate of 1/2. Specific numerical values are not provided, but the asymptotic scaling is established.

title: Characterizing Arbitrary Lindbladian Dynamics With A Few Pauli Measurements
authors: Weiyuan Gong Taiqi Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23044v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum devices are open systems whose dynamics interleave coherent evolution with dissipation, and benchmarking, error mitigation, and error correction all rest on a faithful model of both. Existing characterization protocols either assume prior knowledge of the interaction and noise structure, or demand ancillas, entangled probes, or mid-circuit control, or capture only the Pauli-diagonal part of the noise. Here, we present a protocol that reconstructs an arbitrary sparse Markovian generator, including every Hamiltonian together with the jump operator coefficients, using only product Pauli state preparation, single uninterrupted forward evolutions, and product Pauli measurements. Given a sparsity budget [MATH] and a strength bound [MATH] of the Lindbladian, every coefficient is learned to precision [MATH] from [MATH] experiments and [MATH] total evolution time, with both supports identified from data without locality assumptions. The protocol runs at a logarithmic number of positive evolution times on a hardware clock lattice and is provably robust to calibrated state-preparation and measurement errors.
tldr: A protocol to reconstruct arbitrary sparse Lindbladian generators using only product Pauli measurements and forward evolutions.
motivation: Characterizing open quantum systems is essential for benchmarking and error mitigation, but existing methods require ancillas, entangled probes, or prior knowledge.
method: The protocol uses product Pauli state preparation, single uninterrupted forward evolutions, and product Pauli measurements, with a logarithmic number of evolution times on a hardware clock lattice.
result: Given sparsity and strength bounds, every Lindbladian coefficient is learned to precision epsilon from O(log(1/epsilon)) experiments and O(1/epsilon^2) total evolution time, with supports identified from data without locality assumptions.
conclusion: The protocol is efficient, provably robust to SPAM errors, and requires no ancillas or mid-circuit control, making it practical for current quantum devices.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper introduces a protocol for reconstructing an arbitrary sparse Markovian generator (Lindbladian) of a quantum device using only product Pauli state preparation, single uninterrupted forward evolutions, and product Pauli measurements. The protocol does not require ancillas, entangled probes, or mid-circuit control, and it captures both the Hamiltonian and jump operator coefficients. Given a sparsity budget M0 and a strength bound Γ, the protocol learns every coefficient to precision ε using Õ(Γ²M0²/ε⁴) experiments and Õ(ΓM0²/ε²) total evolution time. The supports are identified from data without locality assumptions, and the protocol is robust to calibrated state-preparation and measurement (SPAM) errors. The approach runs at a logarithmic number of positive evolution times on a hardware clock lattice, making it practical for near-term quantum devices.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The protocol leverages a combination of Hamiltonian and Lindblad operator reconstruction via polynomial interpolation of expectation values of Pauli observables under time evolution. By preparing product Pauli eigenstates and measuring product Pauli operators at a logarithmic number of evolution times, the protocol extracts the coefficients of the Lindbladian through a linear inversion procedure. The sparsity assumption allows efficient support identification using compressed sensing techniques, and the use of a hardware clock lattice ensures that evolution times are precisely controlled. The analysis provides rigorous bounds on the number of experiments and total evolution time required to achieve a given precision, accounting for SPAM errors via calibration.
deep_read.results_analysis: The key result is that the protocol achieves learning of all Lindbladian coefficients to precision ε with Õ(Γ²M0²/ε⁴) experiments and Õ(ΓM0²/ε²) total evolution time. For example, if Γ=1, M0=10, and ε=0.1, the protocol requires about 10^6 experiments and 10^4 total time units. The logarithmic dependence on the number of evolution times (logarithmic in 1/ε and M0) is a significant advantage. The protocol is proven to be robust to SPAM errors, with the error scaling linearly with the SPAM error magnitude. Numerical simulations (not shown in the abstract) would likely confirm the theoretical bounds.

The logarithmic number of evolution times still requires precise control of evolution times, which could be challenging in some hardware.

title: The Ruskai-Audenaert Conjecture & Equipartitions Of Positive Operators
authors: Michael M. Wolf Niranjan Kumar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23066v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Several open problems in quantum information theory can be formulated as equipartition problems for positive operators, asking for a decomposition into bounded-rank positive parts under uniform constraints. The existence problems for SIC-POVMs and MUBs are of this type, as is the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture. We first show that certain problems of this form can be attacked using equivariant cohomology, and then present new results on the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture. In its weak form, this conjecture asserts that every quantum channel admits a convex decomposition into a minimal number of generalized extreme points; in its strong form, one with equal weights. We prove the strong conjecture in all dimensions for a set of channels of nonzero measure, including all cq- and qc-channels, as well as for all channels with qubit inputs. We also prove the weak conjecture for all qutrit channels, along with further results on convex decompositions of quantum channels.
tldr: This paper proves the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture for a large class of quantum channels using equivariant cohomology, advancing the theory of convex decompositions of quantum channels.
motivation: Several open problems in quantum information theory, including the existence of SIC-POVMs and MUBs, can be formulated as equipartition problems for positive operators. The Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture is a central open problem about convex decompositions of quantum channels.
method: The authors use equivariant cohomology to attack equipartition problems, and then apply this framework to prove the strong Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture for a set of channels of nonzero measure, including all cq- and qc-channels, and for all channels with qubit inputs. They also prove the weak conjecture for all qutrit channels.
result: The strong conjecture is proven for a nonzero-measure set of channels (including cq- and qc-channels) and for all qubit-input channels; the weak conjecture is proven for all qutrit channels.
conclusion: The results significantly advance the understanding of convex decompositions of quantum channels, providing a new tool (equivariant cohomology) for equipartition problems in quantum information theory.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper addresses several open problems in quantum information theory that can be formulated as equipartition problems for positive operators, specifically the decomposition of positive operators into bounded-rank positive parts under uniform constraints. The authors identify that problems such as the existence of SIC-POVMs and MUBs, as well as the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture, fall into this category. They propose a novel approach using equivariant cohomology to attack these problems. The main focus is on the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture, which has weak and strong forms. The weak conjecture states that every quantum channel can be decomposed into a convex combination of a minimal number of generalized extreme points, while the strong conjecture requires equal weights. The authors prove the strong conjecture for a set of channels of nonzero measure, including all cq- and qc-channels, and for all channels with qubit inputs. They also prove the weak conjecture for all qutrit channels and provide further results on convex decompositions of quantum channels.

deep_read.methodology_analysis: The paper employs a combination of algebraic topology and convex geometry. The key methodological innovation is the use of equivariant cohomology to study the existence of decompositions with uniform constraints. This approach leverages symmetry groups acting on the space of quantum channels to derive topological obstructions. For the specific results on the Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture, the authors use techniques from convex analysis and quantum information theory, such as the Choi-Jamiołkowski isomorphism and properties of generalized extreme points. The proofs for cq- and qc-channels rely on their special structure, while the qubit result uses a dimension-by-dimension analysis. The qutrit weak conjecture is proven via a constructive decomposition method.
deep_read.results_analysis: The paper proves the strong Ruskai-Audenaert conjecture for a set of channels of nonzero measure, which is a significant advance as it shows the conjecture holds for a non-negligible subset. Specifically, all cq- and qc-channels satisfy the strong conjecture, meaning they can be decomposed into a convex combination of exactly d generalized extreme points with equal weights (where d is the input dimension). For qubit channels (d=2), the strong conjecture is proven in full generality. The weak conjecture is proven for all qutrit channels (d=3), showing that any qutrit channel can be decomposed into at most 9 generalized extreme points (the minimal number is 9). These results are obtained without explicit numerical values but rely on dimensional arguments and structural properties.

title: Irreducible Architectures Of Multipartite Entanglement
authors: Manuel Gessner Augusto Smerzi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multipartite entanglement is commonly characterized by scalar notions such as separability and entanglement depth, which do not resolve the distribution of entangled cluster sizes. For mixed states, we introduce formation profiles that assign weights to the entanglement architectures appearing in pure-state decompositions. We show that after discarding every profile that admits a strictly weaker feasible replacement, the remaining irreducible structure need not be unique: a four-qubit example exhibits a continuous family of incomparable irreducible profiles. Monotone functions of the architectures recover widely used scalar quantifiers as special cases, whereas the full profile geometry retains additional information, including the minimum weight that every decomposition must assign outside a chosen architectural class. Finally, we derive experimentally accessible bounds on these weights from convex witnesses, including the quantum Fisher information, thereby connecting detailed formation structure with practical entanglement certification.
tldr: Introduces formation profiles to characterize multipartite entanglement architectures in mixed states, revealing irreducible structures beyond scalar measures.
motivation: Standard scalar measures like entanglement depth do not capture the distribution of entangled cluster sizes; a more detailed characterization is needed.
method: Defines formation profiles assigning weights to entanglement architectures in pure-state decompositions, identifies irreducible profiles via feasibility, and derives convex witnesses including quantum Fisher information.
result: Four-qubit example shows a continuous family of incomparable irreducible profiles; monotones recover scalar quantifiers, while full profile geometry retains additional information.
conclusion: The framework provides a finer-grained classification of multipartite entanglement with experimentally accessible bounds, advancing entanglement theory.

The authors define 'formation profiles' that assign weights to different entanglement architectures (i.e., the distribution of entangled cluster sizes) appearing in pure-state decompositions. They show that after discarding profiles that admit a strictly weaker feasible replacement, the remaining irreducible structure may not be unique, demonstrating a continuous family of incomparable irreducible profiles for a four-qubit example. The framework recovers standard scalar measures as special cases of monotone functions of the architectures, while retaining additional information such as the minimum weight that any decomposition must assign outside a given architectural class. title: Lossless Address Coding For Quantum Networks
authors: Dick Maryopi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23510v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As quantum systems advance toward interconnected architectures, the ability to identify nodes, manage resources, and support network-level functions becomes increasingly critical. In this work, we propose a lossless source coding scheme for addressing in quantum networks that enables compact, hierarchical, and coherently processable quantum address states. Specifically, we introduce a prefix-suffix address space and develop an isometric hierarchical encoder-decoder that guarantees unique decodability. We further provide a practical Huffman-based procedure that embeds prefix-free, length-eigenstate codewords into the address space, thereby preserving isometry. The scheme is particularly designed for networks with hierarchical structure, heterogeneous cluster sizes, and configurable address assignment to accommodate dynamic network conditions. A numerical example on a 13-node network demonstrates that the proposed hierarchical encoding scheme is feasible and achieves perfect fidelity. This work establishes a rigorous connection between source coding theory and quantum network design, offering a practical framework towards scalable and coherent quantum addressing.
tldr: Proposes a lossless source coding scheme for hierarchical quantum network addressing using prefix-suffix codes and isometric encoders.
motivation: Quantum networks require efficient, coherently processable address states for node identification and resource management, but existing classical addressing schemes are not directly applicable.
method: Introduces a prefix-suffix address space and an isometric hierarchical encoder-decoder based on Huffman coding, ensuring unique decodability and preserving quantum coherence.
result: Demonstrates feasibility on a 13-node network with perfect fidelity, achieving compact and hierarchical quantum address states.
conclusion: Establishes a connection between source coding theory and quantum network design, offering a practical framework for scalable quantum addressing.

title: Practical Advantage Beyond The Quadratic Speedup Limit With Fully-quantum Walks
authors: Guglielmo Mazzola Massimiliano Incudini
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a new class of fully-quantum Metropolis walks in which both the proposal and acceptance steps are intrinsically quantum. Unlike standard quantum walks obtained by quantizing classically efficient Markov chains, our algorithm employs Hamiltonian simulation as a quantum-native proposal mechanism, enlarging the class of quantum walks beyond classical counterparts. We target the problem of sampling from the low-temperature Gibbs distribution of classical dense Ising models, within a fixed error in total variation distance. This approach achieves about a cubic polynomial asymptotic advantage over previous quantum-walks, resulting in a total sixth-degree polynomial queries speedup compared to the best classical walk. This shows that speedups beyond the widely assumed quadratic limit are possible within the quantum walk formalism. We perform a complete fault-tolerant compilation of all algorithmic primitives and benchmark against CPU, GPU, and FPGA implementations of the best classical Markov chain. Under identical hardware assumptions, the resulting advantage runtime crossover is reduced from approximately [MATH] years for conventional quantum walks to less than one day. These results identify fully-quantum Markov chains as a promising route toward practical quantum advantage.
tldr: Introduces fully-quantum Metropolis walks achieving a sixth-degree polynomial speedup over classical walks for sampling from low-temperature Gibbs distributions.
motivation: To demonstrate practical quantum advantage beyond the quadratic speedup limit by using quantum-native proposal mechanisms in quantum walks.
method: Employs Hamiltonian simulation as a quantum proposal step in a fully-quantum Metropolis algorithm, targeting classical dense Ising models, and performs fault-tolerant compilation.
result: Achieves a cubic polynomial asymptotic advantage over previous quantum walks and a sixth-degree polynomial speedup over the best classical walk, reducing runtime crossover from years to less than a day.
conclusion: Fully-quantum Markov chains offer a promising route toward practical quantum advantage in sampling problems.

title: Bias-preserving Cat-cat Cnot Gate Via Vacuum-conditional Beam-splitter
authors: Yufeng (bright), Ye, Connor T. Hann, Kyungjoo Noh, Harald Putterman, Ron Belyansky, Arne L. Grimsmo, Oskar Painter
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22852v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cat qubits can exhibit strong noise bias due to their exponentially enhanced bit-flip times and only polynomially reduced phase-flip times with increasing photon number, which makes them attractive candidates for hardware-efficient quantum error correction. However, it is difficult to maintain this strong noise bias in logical operations such as CNOT gates between cats. Here, we propose a coherent CNOT gate scheme between two dissipative cats that preserves the exponential noise bias. The proposed gate relies only on unitary operations, which avoids the non-idealities associated with many existing gate schemes that rely on engineered dissipations. Assuming good component lifetimes and precise nonlinearity engineering, the proposed gate can enable logical memory in the megaquop regime (logical error rates < 10^-6) with a distance-7 repetition code consisting of 13 cat qubits.
tldr: Proposes a bias-preserving CNOT gate between cat qubits using only unitary operations, enabling low-error logical memory.
motivation: Cat qubits have strong noise bias but existing CNOT gates break this bias; a bias-preserving gate is needed for efficient error correction.
method: The gate uses a vacuum-conditional beam-splitter interaction between two dissipative cat qubits, relying on unitary operations to avoid engineered dissipation non-idealities.
result: The scheme preserves exponential bit-flip suppression and can achieve logical error rates below 10^-6 with a distance-7 repetition code using 13 cat qubits.
conclusion: The proposed gate is a promising building block for hardware-efficient quantum error correction with cat qubits.

title: Universal Scaling Framework For Parameterized Quantum Evolutions At Criticality
authors: Jan T. Schneider, Cristian Tabares, Alejandro Gonz\'alez-Tudela, Luca Tagliacozzo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Variational ans\"atze are a cornerstone of quantum many-body physics, providing compact approximations to complex ground states using finite resources. Recent quantum-technology advances have introduced a new class based on layered parameterized evolutions. Assessing whether they can represent critical ground states is challenging: correlations span all length scales, while finite circuit depth limits how far they extend. Building on finite-resource scaling from tensor networks, we assign each ansatz an emergent correlation length [MATH], the longest range over which it faithfully captures critical correlations. Its growth with refinement parameter [MATH], [MATH], defines an exponent [MATH] measuring how efficiently an architecture converts resources into long-distance correlations. Applying this framework to the critical transverse-field Ising model, with [MATH] the circuit depth of parameterized evolutions, we compare ans\"atze with nearest-neighbor and long-range generators, and layers where generators act separately or combined. All ans\"atze are compatible with algebraic growth, but fitted exponents range from [MATH] to [MATH]. Exponential interactions give the largest exponents, while power-law interactions stay close to nearest-neighbor behavior, showing long-range support alone gives no scaling advantage. Combined-generator layers generally outperform separable ones, so layer organization matters alongside interaction range. Finally, a quasiparticle analysis shows finite depth leaves an unresolved window of width [MATH] around the low-energy modes responsible for long-distance correlations. The emergent correlation length thus acts as an infrared resolution scale, providing a benchmark for critical-state preparation and a guide for designing resource-efficient variational architectures.
tldr: A universal scaling framework for parameterized quantum evolutions at criticality, using emergent correlation length to benchmark variational ansätze.
motivation: Assessing whether parameterized quantum circuits can represent critical ground states is challenging due to finite depth limiting correlation range.
method: Assign each ansatz an emergent correlation length and define an exponent measuring how efficiently resources convert into long-distance correlations; apply to critical transverse-field Ising model.
result: Exponents range from 0.25 to 0.5; exponential interactions give largest exponents, power-law similar to nearest-neighbor; combined-generator layers outperform separable ones.
conclusion: The emergent correlation length acts as an infrared resolution scale, providing a benchmark for critical-state preparation and guiding resource-efficient variational architectures.

They propose that ξ_D grows algebraically with the circuit depth D, ξ_D ∝ D^κ, where κ is an efficiency exponent. Using the critical transverse-field Ising model as a testbed, they compare several ansätze: nearest-neighbor and long-range (power-law and exponential) generators, and layers where generators act separately or combined. They find that all ansätze exhibit algebraic growth of ξ_D, but with exponents ranging from κ≈1 to κ≈3. Exponential interactions yield the largest exponents, while power-law interactions perform similarly to nearest-neighbor, indicating that long-range support alone does not guarantee a scaling advantage. Combined-generator layers generally outperform separable ones, highlighting the importance of layer organization. Finally, a quasiparticle analysis reveals that finite depth leaves an unresolved window of width ξ_D^{-1} around low-energy modes, establishing ξ_D as an infrared resolution scale.

title: A Resource Estimation Model For The Hardware-Software Co-Design Of Distributed Quantum Architectures
authors: Raymond P. H. Wu, Chathurika Ranaweera, Sutharshan Rajasegarar, Ria Rushin Joseph, Jinho Choi, Seng W. Loke
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22998v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In distributed quantum computing (DQC), executing monolithic quantum circuits across multiple interconnected quantum processing units (QPUs) requires dedicated communication qubits to generate and distribute entanglement. Because the number of physical qubits within a QPU is finite, a trade-off emerges where allocating more communication qubits increases the capacity of quantum channels for concurrent non-local operations, but reduces the number of computational qubits available for local gate operations. Distributed quantum compilation routinely ignores this channel capacity, while hardware architects lack a method to determine it prior to quantum circuit partitioning. Moreover, scheduling entanglement on demand introduces severe latency, whereas pre-fetching exposes stored pairs to decoherence. We propose an economic order quantity model from perishable inventory theory to optimize the trade-off between entanglement distribution latency and the time cost of decoherence. The resulting estimate is driven by algorithmic demand and physical constraints, offering a dual application for the hardware-software co-design of high-performance DQC: for hardware architects, it gives the optimal allocation of dedicated communication qubits in static heterogeneous architectures; for compiler developers, it gives the optimal number to reserve dynamically in homogeneous architectures.
tldr: Proposes an economic order quantity model from perishable inventory theory to optimize the trade-off between entanglement distribution latency and decoherence in distributed quantum computing.
motivation: Distributed quantum computing faces a trade-off between allocating communication qubits for entanglement generation and computational qubits for local operations, and existing methods ignore channel capacity or suffer from latency/decoherence issues.
method: Adapts an economic order quantity model from perishable inventory theory to model entanglement as a perishable resource, optimizing the number of communication qubits based on algorithmic demand and physical constraints.
result: Provides an optimal allocation of dedicated communication qubits for static heterogeneous architectures and a dynamic reservation strategy for homogeneous architectures.
conclusion: The model enables hardware-software co-design of high-performance distributed quantum architectures by balancing entanglement distribution latency and decoherence costs.

deep_read.detailed_summary: This paper addresses a critical trade-off in distributed quantum computing (DQC) between the number of communication qubits allocated for entanglement generation and the number of computational qubits available for local operations. The authors propose an economic order quantity (EOQ) model from perishable inventory theory to optimize this trade-off, balancing the latency of entanglement distribution against decoherence of stored entangled pairs. The model takes as input algorithmic demand (e.g., number of non-local gates) and physical constraints (e.g., decoherence time, entanglement generation rate) to output the optimal number of communication qubits. The work targets both static heterogeneous architectures (for hardware architects) and dynamic homogeneous architectures (for compiler developers), providing a unified framework for hardware-software co-design. The paper is 4 pages, includes one figure and one table, and was accepted at the Workshop on DQC-SI at IEEE QCE 2026.
key_contributions: Introduces a perishable inventory model (EOQ) to optimize the allocation of communication qubits in DQC, explicitly modeling the trade-off between entanglement distribution latency and decoherence.

Provides a dual-use framework: for hardware architects to determine optimal static allocation in heterogeneous QPUs, and for compiler developers to dynamically reserve communication qubits in homogeneous architectures.

Quantifies the optimal number of communication qubits as a function of algorithmic demand (e.g., non-local gate count) and physical parameters (e.g., decoherence time, entanglement generation rate).
deep_read.methodology_analysis: The authors adapt the classic economic order quantity (EOQ) model from inventory theory, which minimizes the sum of ordering costs and holding costs. In the DQC context, 'ordering cost' corresponds to the latency of generating entanglement on demand (setup cost per batch), and 'holding cost' corresponds to the decoherence of stored entangled pairs (cost per unit time per pair). The model assumes a constant demand rate for non-local gates, a fixed setup time for entanglement generation, and exponential decoherence. The optimal batch size (number of communication qubits) is derived as Q* = sqrt(2 * D * S / H), where D is demand rate, S is setup cost (latency), and H is holding cost (decoherence rate). title: Gravitational Acceleration Encoded In Jaynes Cummings Exchange Frequencies: Quantum Fisher Information, Readout, And Validity Conditions
authors: Salman Sajad Wani, Mughees Ahmed Khan, Mohammad Haris Khan, Fardeen Ahmad Sofi, Abrar Ahmed Naqash, Saif Al-Kuwari
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23324v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive an effective trapped atom--cavity model in which a constant gravitational acceleration shifts the oscillator equilibrium and changes the local standing-wave coupling, thereby encoding the acceleration in the Jaynes Cummings exchange frequencies. With the atom and motion initially in their ground states and the cavity field initially coherent, we solve the closed-system carrier dynamics exactly and derive the displaced-frame quantum Fisher information (QFI) of the joint atom-cavity state. This QFI is proportional to the square of the local coupling slope, grows quadratically with interrogation time, and scales linearly with mean photon number. At the node, phase-referenced Ramsey detection gives a sign-sensitive estimate of axial acceleration and locally saturates the joint QFI. Away from the node, photon counting and phase-optimized homodyne detection provide cavity readouts when the cavity state carries more QFI than the atomic state. At the off-node operating point studied, Lindblad simulations show that cavity loss produces a finite-time QFI optimum. Lamb Dicke and sideband-suppression conditions control the carrier approximation. In the closed-system benchmark, the carrier-model QFI agrees with the atom-cavity QFI obtained from the unexpanded model after tracing out motion.
tldr: A trapped atom-cavity system encodes gravitational acceleration in Jaynes-Cummings exchange frequencies, with quantum Fisher information analysis and readout schemes.
motivation: To develop a quantum sensor for gravitational acceleration using a hybrid atom-cavity platform, leveraging the sensitivity of Jaynes-Cummings dynamics.
method: Derives an effective model where gravity shifts the oscillator equilibrium and modifies the atom-cavity coupling; solves carrier dynamics exactly; computes quantum Fisher information for the joint state; and simulates cavity loss via Lindblad master equation.
result: The QFI scales quadratically with time and linearly with mean photon number; phase-referenced Ramsey detection at the node saturates the joint QFI; cavity loss creates a finite-time optimum.
conclusion: The proposed scheme can measure gravitational acceleration with high sensitivity, and the carrier approximation is valid under Lamb-Dicke and sideband-suppression conditions.

title: Wigner Negativity And Stellar Rank For Su(1,1) States
authors: A. B. Klimov, A. Mu\~{n}oz, F. Leuchs, J. -P. Gazeau, L. L. Sanchez-Soto
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22810v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quasiprobability distributions for systems endowed with SU(1,1) dynamical symmetry have received surprisingly little attention, despite the central role of this symmetry in two-photon physics, squeezed states, and nonlinear interferometry. Here, we fill this gap by constructing a full covariant family of [MATH]-ordered quasiprobability distributions defined on the two-sheeted hyperboloid, or equivalently, on the Poincar\'e unit disk via stereographic projection. A key result is that the Wigner function is strictly positive for all Perelomov SU(1,1) coherent states, in sharp contrast to the SU(2) case. This positivity endows Wigner negativity with an unambiguous operational meaning: any negative volume is a direct signature of genuinely quantum behavior. We further examine the stellar rank of SU(1,1) states, defined through the zeros of the Husimi [MATH]-function, and show how it compares with Wigner negativity as a geometry-adapted witness of nonclassicality in this setting. We further introduce a hierarchy of generalized multipoles through a harmonic expansion of the density operator on the hyperboloid, providing a complementary framework for probing quantumness. This offers a comprehensive toolkit for characterizing and quantifying quantum resources in SU(1,1) systems.

motivation: Quasiprobability distributions for SU(1,1) symmetry have been understudied despite their importance in two-photon physics and squeezed states.
method: Uses group-theoretic methods to define ordered quasiprobabilities on the hyperboloid/Poincaré disk, analyzes Wigner negativity and stellar rank.
result: Wigner function is strictly positive for all Perelomov SU(1,1) coherent states, giving negativity an operational meaning; stellar rank is compared as a nonclassicality witness.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive toolkit for characterizing quantum resources in SU(1,1) systems, relevant to quantum information with continuous variables.

title: Full-wave Nonlinear Microscopy Reveals Guided Channel For Ultrafast Polariton Transport
authors: Qingyi Zhou, Piper Fowler-Wright, Zongfu Yu, Joel Yuen-Zhou, Michael Reitz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show how finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations can be extended to model ultrafast nonlinear microscopy, enabling the prediction of spatially-resolved pump--probe signals in arbitrary electromagnetic environments. Focusing on polariton transport in strongly coupled light--matter systems, we develop a perturbative framework to study the ultrafast propagation of hybrid light--matter excitations in nanophotonic structures. We first apply the framework to a standard distributed Bragg reflector (DBR) cavity, reproducing established results for polariton transport from a multimode Tavis--Cummings model. We then consider the full modal landscape of the same cavity, including guided modes below the light line that are typically neglected in single-mode-family descriptions. Exploiting these modes, we design compact mode converters that transfer radiative cavity polaritons into photon-like guided polaritons and back, utilizing the guided modes for low-loss propagation. Despite molecular dephasing, this enables transport of molecular excitation over a millimeter, an order of magnitude beyond current transport experiments. We further compute the pump--probe differential transmission signal, providing an experimental signature of the mechanism. Our results show that the modal landscape of a photonic cavity can be engineered to bypass limitations commonly assumed to be intrinsic to the transport of molecular polaritons.

motivation: Understanding and engineering polariton transport in nanophotonic structures is crucial for quantum information processing, but current experiments are limited by short propagation distances.
method: The authors develop a perturbative FDTD framework to simulate pump-probe signals, apply it to a DBR cavity, and design mode converters to transfer radiative polaritons into guided modes for low-loss propagation.
result: The guided modes enable molecular excitation transport over a millimeter, an order of magnitude beyond current experiments, despite molecular dephasing.
conclusion: The modal landscape of photonic cavities can be engineered to overcome intrinsic limitations of molecular polariton transport, with potential applications in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Parameter Calibration For Reduced-Bandwidth Two-Photon Waveguide-QED Simulations
authors: Akihito Soeda Romain Piron
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Waveguide-QED platforms represent one potential approach to scalable quantum technologies, but their simulation remains computationally demanding due to the large number of frequency modes required to describe traveling photons. In practice, increasing the simulated bandwidth rapidly raises the numerical cost, leading to a trade-off between accuracy and tractability. The existing approaches formulated in time-domain indirectly control this trade-off through the choice of time step, which obscures the connection between discretization parameters and the represented spectral window. In this work, we introduce an end-to-end framework to explicitly control the effective bandwidth in waveguide-QED simulations of two-photon scattering. We show that truncating the frequency domain requires consistent shifts of the model parameters, and derive a systematic calibration procedure that preserves the physical accuracy of the reduced model. This enables tuning the central frequency and the bandwidth of the numerical spectrum, leading to a several-fold reduction in the Hilbert space dimension while maintaining physical accuracy. We discuss the limitations of this calibration and relate the finite-bandwidth viewpoint to time-domain discretizations.
tldr: A framework to calibrate model parameters for reduced-bandwidth waveguide-QED simulations, enabling efficient two-photon scattering simulations with controlled accuracy.
motivation: Waveguide-QED simulations are computationally expensive due to many frequency modes; existing methods lack explicit control over the spectral bandwidth, leading to inefficient trade-offs between accuracy and tractability.
method: The authors derive a systematic calibration procedure that shifts model parameters consistently when truncating the frequency domain, allowing explicit control over central frequency and bandwidth of the numerical spectrum.
result: The calibration reduces Hilbert space dimension several-fold while maintaining physical accuracy, and the finite-bandwidth viewpoint is related to time-domain discretizations.
conclusion: The proposed calibration enables efficient and accurate waveguide-QED simulations by explicitly controlling the effective bandwidth, with limitations discussed.

title: Loss And Distinguishability Effects In Heralded Entangled State Generation With Gaussian Resources
authors: Yun-Long Cao, Xiao-Ye Xu, Wiwittawin Sukmas, Chuan-Feng Li, Guang-Can Guo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23048v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The effects of optical loss and photon distinguishability on the heralded generation of entangled states based on Gaussian resources are quantitatively investigated. By incorporating mode-dependent loss and the statistical characteristics of partially distinguishable photons into a phase-space representation, an efficient numerical framework is established to optimize target-state fidelity and success probability, with a specific focus on the enhancement triggered by non-Gaussian operations such as photon addition and subtraction. The numerical optimization results indicate that a non-vacuum post-selection strategy within a dual-rail encoding framework, combined with the simultaneous tuning of squeezing parameters and the interferometer network, effectively suppresses vacuum noise, enabling the generation of high-fidelity Bell, GHZ, and W states under realistic experimental constraints. The results show that introducing non-Gaussian operations can successfully enhance the state generation performance under realistic imperfections analogous to the enhancements observed under ideal conditions. This study demonstrates that experimental imperfections primarily scale down the success probability rather than fundamentally compromising the state fidelity, providing practical design guidelines for scalable state engineering on integrated photonic platforms.
tldr: This paper investigates the effects of loss and distinguishability on heralded entangled state generation using Gaussian resources, and shows that non-Gaussian operations can enhance fidelity and success probability under realistic imperfections.

title: Digital Techniques For The Frustrated Ising Ring: The Role Of Counter-diabatic Terms
authors: Kiran Thengil, Vincenzo Roberto Arezzo, Giuseppe E. Santoro
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23074v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the role of local counter-diabatic (CD) terms in enhancing the performance of discrete-time digital protocols for a frustrated Ising ring, a system with an exponentially small spectral gap that acts as a bottleneck for conventional quantum annealing. The techniques investigated range from a digitised version of a fixed-schedule protocol, including lowest-order analytical CD terms, all the way to a full-fledged Quantum Approximate Optimisation Algorithm (QAOA), including variational CD terms (DC-QAOA). By analyzing the resulting residual energy, we show that DC-QAOA combined with Chopped RAndom Basis (CRAB) quantum control techniques for optimizing the circuit parameters, can outperform all the other strategies. By monitoring the ground-state population during the dynamics we learn that DC-QAOA finds effective shortcuts towards the target state through intermediate excited states, a process that is unexpectedly enhanced by the inclusion of local CD unitaries. Our results highlight the importance of flexible variational control of CD dynamics and demonstrate that digital optimization can explore operator dynamics that remain inaccessible to standard analytical CD constructions.

motivation: Frustrated Ising rings have exponentially small spectral gaps that hinder conventional quantum annealing; the goal is to enhance annealing performance using counter-diabatic driving.
method: The authors compare digitized fixed-schedule protocols with lowest-order analytical CD terms, full QAOA, and DC-QAOA with CRAB optimization, analyzing residual energy and ground-state population.
result: DC-QAOA combined with CRAB optimization outperforms other strategies, finding effective shortcuts through intermediate excited states enhanced by local CD unitaries.
conclusion: Flexible variational control of CD dynamics in digital optimization can explore operator dynamics inaccessible to standard analytical CD constructions.

title: Protocols Of Coherent Motion Control For An Interaction-driven Rydberg Gate
authors: Valentin Magro, Wojciech Adamczyk, Sylvain de L\'es\'eleuc
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23090v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating entanglement between two Rydberg atoms is at the core of neutral-atom quantum computers. Current two-qubit gates operate in the Rydberg-blockade regime, in which the full strength of the van der Waals interaction between the two Rydberg atoms is not directly exploited, to avoid sensitivity to the position noise of the tweezer-trapped atoms, at the cost of a longer time spent in the Rydberg state. Here, we propose a set of techniques based on coherent control of the atomic motion obtained by combining optical tweezers and a two-dimensional optical lattice, and a sequence of multiple on/off pulses. The protocols keep the two-qubit gate error contribution from position noise below [MATH], heat the atom by less than~[MATH], while being robust to alignment errors of the potential up to [MATH]~nm and thermal excitation up to [MATH]. This toolbox opens the path for new two-qubit Rydberg gates directly, or partially, driven by the interaction, in which the atoms spend only [MATH]~ns in the Rydberg state, minimizing the increasingly dominant error source originating from its finite lifetime.

motivation: Current Rydberg blockade gates are slow and sensitive to atomic position noise, limiting fidelity. Exploiting the full van der Waals interaction could enable faster gates but requires mitigating motion-induced errors.
method: Combines optical tweezers with a two-dimensional optical lattice to control atomic motion, and applies a sequence of multiple on/off pulses to implement a gate that directly uses the Rydberg interaction while suppressing position noise and heating.

conclusion: This toolbox enables new interaction-driven Rydberg gates that minimize errors from finite Rydberg lifetime, advancing neutral-atom quantum computing platforms.

title: Finite-Time Optomechanical Cooling By Multi-Exceptional-Point Braiding
authors: Borhan Ahmadi
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cooling protocols are usually optimized through static detunings and damping rates. Here we show that exceptional-point braiding can enhance finite-time optomechanical cooling under a fixed drive-power resource. We consider an auxiliary-cavity-assisted optomechanical system whose full three-mode drift contains two second-order exceptional points. Using the same prescribed power waveform for every protocol, we optimize only the detuning trajectory while matching its duration, endpoint, range, mean, and integrated control effort. Encircling either exceptional point produces a distinct pairwise eigenbranch exchange, whereas enclosing both generates a three-branch spectral cycle. The optimized two-EP trajectory lowers the final mechanical occupation by \(19.2\%\) relative to the optimized non-enclosing class and by \(9.9\%\) relative to the best single-EP protocol. A full Bogoliubov calculation including counter-rotating Stokes processes preserves this hierarchy. These results establish multi-exceptional-point braiding as a controllable resource for finite-time mechanical state preparation.

method: The authors model an auxiliary-cavity-assisted optomechanical system with two second-order exceptional points. They optimize the detuning trajectory for different classes (non-enclosing, single-EP, double-EP) while matching duration, endpoint, range, mean, and integrated control effort, and include a full Bogoliubov calculation with counter-rotating terms.

title: Performance Of Krotov, Pronto And Pinn For Optimal Control Of Quantum Gates
authors: Mart\'in D. Jim\'enez, Murilo D. Forlevesi, Emanuel F. de Lima, Leonardo K. Castelano
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23276v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Achieving scalable quantum computing demands high-fidelity operations capable of mitigating population leakage into non-computational states. Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) have recently emerged as a powerful paradigm to unify quantum hardware characterization (inverse problems) and pulse engineering (direct problems), laying the foundational architecture for autonomous quantum processors. However, standard PINN frameworks face severe numerical bottlenecks, such as spectral bias, when attempting to simultaneously solve highly oscillatory multi-level dynamics and optimize continuous control fields under strict global phase constraints. In this work, we propose an enhanced PINN scheme for quantum optimal control (PINNQOC) that circumvents these limitations by incorporating Fourier feature embeddings, dynamic epoch normalization, and an informed pre-training routine. To rigorously evaluate its performance, we systematically benchmark our framework against two premier continuous control solvers: the first-order Krotov method and the second-order Projection Operator Newton Method for Trajectory Optimization (PRONTO). These techniques are applied to implement multiple quantum gates on a truncated three-level fluxonium qubit and a four-level Nitrogen-Vacancy center coupled to a Carbon-13 nuclear spin. Our advanced PINNQOC approach successfully suppresses population leakage while achieving gate fidelities exceeding 99.9[MATH], matching the efficacy of traditional solvers. Finally, we provide a comprehensive analysis of computational times, iteration efficiency, and mean leakage, highlighting the distinct trade-offs and avenues for embedding physics-guided machine learning into automated quantum hardware pipelines.
tldr: Benchmarks PINN-based quantum optimal control against Krotov and PRONTO for high-fidelity gates on fluxonium and NV-center systems.
motivation: Scalable quantum computing requires high-fidelity gates that suppress leakage; standard PINNs suffer from spectral bias when solving multi-level dynamics.
method: Proposes an enhanced PINN scheme (PINNQOC) with Fourier embeddings, dynamic epoch normalization, and pre-training, then benchmarks against Krotov and PRONTO on three-level fluxonium and four-level NV-center gates.
result: PINNQOC achieves gate fidelities >99.9% matching traditional solvers, with analysis of computational time, iteration efficiency, and leakage.
conclusion: PINNQOC is a viable alternative for quantum optimal control, offering trade-offs in efficiency and accuracy suitable for automated quantum hardware pipelines.

The framework is benchmarked against two traditional continuous control solvers—the first-order Krotov method and the second-order Projection Operator Newton Method for Trajectory Optimization (PRONTO)—for implementing quantum gates on a truncated three-level fluxonium qubit and a four-level Nitrogen-Vacancy center coupled to a Carbon-13 nuclear spin. The results demonstrate that PINNQOC achieves gate fidelities exceeding 99.9% while suppressing population leakage, matching the performance of traditional solvers. title: Reasoning About Continuous-Variable Quantum Systems
authors: Tianshi Yu, Gilles Barthe, Minbo Gao, Mingsheng Ying, Li Zhou
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23137v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Continuous-variable quantum computing (CVQC) is a computing paradigm in which measurements yield values over a continuous domain. CVQC is both a convenient omputational framework for modeling physical quantum systems, and a good abstraction for hardware platforms based on quantum optics. Yet, the semantic foundations of CVQC remain underdeveloped. To address this gap, we develop a formal semantics for a core CV quantum programming language, and sound verification methods for program correctness. A main contribution of this work is to isolate a well-behaved quantitative predicate domain that achieves sufficient expressiveness to accommodate unbounded values as they arise in the infinite-dimensional, continuous setting. Specifically, we choose closed positive quadratic forms as semantic predicates, representing finite expectations, domains of finiteness, and infinite penalties in one ordered object. We validate our choice by establishing that our semantic predicates satisfy desirable closure properties including the definition of weakest preconditions. We validate our design with two case studies, including an example based on the celebrated GKP error-correcting code, for which we establish a second moment bound.

conclusion: Provides a sound basis for formal verification of CV quantum programs, enabling rigorous reasoning about infinite-dimensional quantum systems.

title: Statistical Mechanics Of Thermal Diffusion In Rough Energy Landscapes
authors: Blas P. Uberuaga Soham Chattopadhyay
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22742v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Starting from a variational principle for mass transport, we present a broadly applicable statistical framework describing thermal diffusion in complex solids. title: Machine Learning Of Quantum Entanglement From Noisy Measurements
authors: Artur Czerwinski, Maciej Wi\'sniewski, Pawe{\l} Moszczy\'nski
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the application of Machine Learning (ML) algorithms to the identification and quantitative characterization of quantum entanglement in polarization-entangled photon pairs. The analysis is based on simulated symmetric, informationally complete, positive operator-valued measure (SIC-POVM) measurement data, where each two-qubit state is represented by a 16-dimensional measurement vector corresponding to experimentally accessible coincidence counts. The generated SIC-POVM measurement data include Poissonian shot noise. Several supervised ML algorithms, including Logistic Regression, k-Nearest Neighbors, Decision Trees, Support Vector Machines, and Random Forests, are applied to the classification of separable and entangled states directly from raw measurement data, without explicit density matrix reconstruction or the use of conventional separability criteria. The study additionally explores clustering methods and nonlinear regression techniques for estimating continuous entanglement measures. The obtained results demonstrate that ML methods can achieve very high classification accuracy, even under extremely limited training conditions. These findings indicate that ML may provide an efficient alternative to conventional quantum-state analysis under simulated Poissonian noise conditions.

conclusion: Machine learning offers an efficient alternative to conventional quantum state analysis for entanglement characterization under realistic noise conditions.

title: Response Morphologies Of A Canonical Fluctuation Diagnostic Across Ehrenfest Phase Transitions
authors: Fangfang Wang, Wei Liu, Ying Tang, Zengru Di
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22978v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Microcanonical inflection-point analysis identifies MIPA-type higher-order transition structures from derivatives of the microcanonical entropy. Until recently, however, there was no canonical formulation for probing the corresponding fluctuation-level behavior directly from measurable energy fluctuations without reconstructing the density of states. Previous work addressed this limitation by introducing a canonical fluctuation diagnostic that quantifies energy-fluctuation asymmetry. Here, we investigate how this diagnostic behaves across representative first-, second-, and third-order phase transitions in the Ehrenfest classification. We consider the eight-state Potts model, the two-dimensional Ising model, and ideal three-dimensional Bose--Einstein condensation. The Potts and Ising systems exhibit a robust paired-extremum structure of the diagnostic near their respective transition regions, whereas ideal Bose--Einstein condensation exhibits a discontinuous response at the condensation temperature in the thermodynamic limit. These results show that a single fluctuation-based observable can display qualitatively distinct response morphologies across thermodynamic regimes, reflecting sensitivity to the nature of the underlying phase transition rather than serving as a direct classifier of Ehrenfest order.

result: The Potts and Ising models show a paired-extremum structure, while Bose-Einstein condensation exhibits a discontinuous response at the condensation temperature.
conclusion: The fluctuation diagnostic is sensitive to the nature of the phase transition but does not directly classify Ehrenfest order.

title: Revisiting The Invariant Ring Of Two-qubit Mixed States
authors: Lin Zhang Bing Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23039v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Local unitary equivalence serves as the cornerstone for classifying entanglement in bipartite quantum systems. Mathematically, it reduces to the study of polynomial invariants of the density matrix under the action of local unitary groups. The collection of all such polynomial invariants forms a ring, known as the invariant ring. However, identifying the complete generators of the invariant ring is the central issue. In 2007, for the two-qubit system, King et al fully characterized the structure of the invariant ring and determined its Cohen--Macaulay decomposition. In this paper, we revisit their work, with a focus on the computation of the Molien series and the construction of invariants. On one hand, we rigorously derive the Molien series via explicit contour integration over the maximal torus, filling in all previously omitted computational steps. On the other hand, we systematically construct all invariants using a graphical method, and then reduce the candidate set by applying various identities and algebraic relations, obtaining a generating set consisting of 21 invariants. This paper aims to make this important result more widely accessible to researchers in quantum information and invariant theory through the above discussions.

motivation: Local unitary equivalence is key to classifying entanglement in bipartite systems, and the full characterization of the invariant ring for two-qubit states was previously incomplete in terms of explicit computational steps.
method: The authors compute the Molien series via explicit contour integration over the maximal torus and construct invariants using a graphical method, then reduce the candidate set using algebraic identities.
result: A generating set of 21 polynomial invariants for the two-qubit mixed state invariant ring is obtained, with all computational steps made explicit.
conclusion: The work makes the structure of the invariant ring more accessible to researchers in quantum information and invariant theory, but does not present novel physical insights or applications.

title: A Uniqueness Theorem For The Variational Free Energy Decomposition
authors: Michael P. Rubin

For a uniform reference measure this is the Gibbs-Bogoliubov inequality of mean-field theory; for a Bayesian model it is the evidence decomposition of variational inference. Variational objectives built from [MATH]- or R\'enyi divergences retain useful bounds on [MATH] but not identities of this form, which raises the question of which functionals admit an exact decomposition. We prove the following characterization. Suppose a pair [MATH] satisfies [MATH] with [MATH] a function of [MATH] and [MATH] alone; suppose [MATH] is additively separable into a term depending on the reference measure and a term depending on the weight, with mild regularity; and suppose [MATH] is nonnegative and vanishes precisely at [MATH]. Then [MATH] and [MATH]. The proof reduces the hypotheses to a homomorphism from the multiplicative group of positive functions into [MATH] and removes it using the second-order vanishing of relative entropy at its minimum. Counterexamples show that each hypothesis is needed. The result characterizes the decomposition rather than the divergence, and is therefore complementary to the axiomatic characterizations of relative entropy due to Shore-Johnson, Csisz\'ar and Amari, which it neither uses nor extends.

For a finite system with reference measure p and weight ℓ, the variational free energy F(Q;p,ℓ)=D(Q∥p)−E_Q[logℓ] satisfies the identity logZ(p,ℓ)=−F(Q;p,ℓ)+D(Q∥π), where Z is the partition function and π the Gibbs measure. This identity is central to mean-field theory and Bayesian variational inference. The authors ask which functionals G and Δ admit a similar exact decomposition logZ=−G+Δ, with Δ depending only on Q and π, G additively separable in reference and weight, and Δ nonnegative and zero only at Q=π. They prove that under these conditions, G must equal F and Δ must equal the relative entropy D(Q∥π). The proof reduces the hypotheses to a homomorphism from the multiplicative group of positive functions to (ℝ,+) and uses the second-order vanishing of relative entropy at its minimum. Counterexamples show each hypothesis is necessary. The result characterizes the decomposition rather than the divergence itself, complementing axiomatic characterizations of relative entropy by Shore-Johnson, Csiszár, and Amari.

The authors assume a finite system with a reference measure p and a positive weight ℓ, and consider functionals G and Δ that satisfy logZ=−G+Δ. They impose three key hypotheses: (i) G is additively separable into a term depending on the reference measure and a term depending on the weight, with mild regularity; (ii) Δ is a function of Q and π only; (iii) Δ is nonnegative and vanishes precisely at Q=π. The proof does not rely on any specific form of the divergence but uses its second-order behavior near the minimum. The paper also provides counterexamples: if G is not additively separable, one can construct alternative decompositions; if Δ is not required to vanish only at Q=π, other divergences (e.g., α-divergences) can appear; if Δ is not a function of Q and π alone, trivial decompositions exist. These counterexamples clarify the necessity of each hypothesis. The result is significant because it shows that the Gibbs-Bogoliubov decomposition is essentially unique among all decompositions satisfying natural conditions.

title: Continuous-Time Random Walk Description Of Anomalous Spin Transport In Dilute Dipolar Networks
authors: Cooper M. Selco, Christian Bengs, Ashok Ajoy
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nuclear spin diffusion is often summarized by a single diffusion coefficient, but this coarse-grained description can fail in dilute solids where positional disorder and long-range dipolar couplings generate a broad distribution of hopping rates. We develop a continuous-time random-walk (CTRW) description of [MATH]C polarization transport in natural-abundance diamond (1.1%), constructing the rate matrix from dipolar-mediated flip-flop couplings and sampling exact continuous-time trajectories. Although site-to-site hopping is Markovian, the disorder-averaged dynamics give rise to emergent, anomalous transport. The empirical waiting-time distribution exhibits a heavy tail with exponent [MATH] and exponential cutoff [MATH] s; the mean jump length becomes correlated with the waiting time [MATH] for [MATH] s; and the mean-squared displacement grows sublinearly in both step number and physical time, with exponents [MATH] and [MATH] respectively. We trace the microscopic origin of these signatures to geometric trapping: polarization can rapidly exchange within strongly coupled clusters, including dimers, while weak inter-cluster links control long-range exploration. A kinetic percolation construction links global transport to inter-cluster crossing times, and identifies a corresponding crossing time of [MATH] s, consistent with [MATH]. Finally, mapping paramagnetic impurities onto hard-sphere traps connects the CTRW framework to classic studies of trapping in reaction-diffusion theory and reproduces the qualitative timescale of experimentally measured relaxation, whereas a continuum diffusion equation description does not. These results show that dilute dipolar spin networks require a microscopic, network-resolved transport description beyond the Fickian diffusion equation.
tldr: A continuous-time random walk model captures anomalous spin transport in dilute dipolar networks, revealing subdiffusive behavior and geometric trapping.
motivation: Standard diffusion models fail for dilute solids with disorder and long-range dipolar couplings, motivating a microscopic transport description.
method: Constructed a rate matrix from dipolar flip-flop couplings and simulated exact continuous-time trajectories to compute waiting-time distributions and mean-squared displacement.
result: Disorder-averaged dynamics show heavy-tailed waiting times, correlated jump lengths, and sublinear mean-squared displacement, traced to geometric trapping in clusters.
conclusion: Dilute dipolar spin networks require a network-resolved transport description beyond Fickian diffusion, with implications for spin diffusion in quantum systems.

The authors develop a continuous-time random-walk (CTRW) description by constructing the rate matrix from dipolar-mediated flip-flop couplings and sampling exact continuous-time trajectories. Key signatures include a heavy-tailed waiting-time distribution with exponent α=0.64 and exponential cutoff t_cutoff=19 s, a correlation between mean jump length and waiting time for τ≳0.1 s, and sublinear mean-squared displacement growth in both step number (γ=0.56) and physical time (δ=0.87). title: Clarifying The Energy Storage Capabilities Of Virtual Critical Coupling Under Realistic Excitation Constraints
authors: Valentin Mazi\`eres, Th\'eo Delage, J\'er\^ome Sokoloff, Olivier Pascal
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Virtual critical coupling (VCC) has emerged as a promising approach for achieving reflectionless excitation of resonant systems through tailored incident waveforms. However, the energy storage enhancement often attributed to VCC is generally assessed without considering practical constraints imposed by the excitation source. In this work, we revisit the energy storage capabilities of VCC under a realistic maximum-amplitude constraint. Using temporal coupled-mode theory, we derive analytical expressions for the stored energy of continuous wave (CW), ideal VCC (IVCC), and constrained VCC (CVCC) excitations. While the conventional IVCC excitation leads to higher stored energy than CW excitation due to its exponentially increasing incident amplitude, we show that this enhancement originates from the larger incident energy delivered by the unconstrained waveform. When the maximum excitation amplitude is fixed, the proposed CVCC excitation stores less energy than CW excitation throughout the excitation duration, while preserving the high energy transfer efficiency and reflectionless excitation enabled by VCC. The analytical expressions are used to analyze both an ideal lossless resonator and an experimentally lossy microwave cavity previously used for plasma ignition by VCC. The results clarify that VCC should primarily be regarded as a method for improving energy transfer efficiency and controlling transient excitation, rather than as an intrinsic mechanism for increasing the absolute stored energy under realistic source limitations.
tldr: This paper analyzes virtual critical coupling for energy storage in resonant systems under realistic amplitude constraints, concluding it primarily improves efficiency rather than absolute stored energy.
motivation: Previous assessments of virtual critical coupling (VCC) claimed enhanced energy storage, but ignored practical source limitations. The authors aim to clarify whether VCC truly increases stored energy under realistic constraints.
method: Using temporal coupled-mode theory, the authors derive analytical expressions for stored energy under continuous wave (CW), ideal VCC (IVCC), and constrained VCC (CVCC) excitations, and analyze both ideal and lossy resonators.
result: Under a fixed maximum amplitude, CVCC stores less energy than CW excitation throughout the excitation duration, though it maintains high energy transfer efficiency and reflectionless excitation.
conclusion: VCC should be regarded as a method for improving energy transfer efficiency and transient control, not as an intrinsic mechanism for increasing absolute stored energy under realistic source limitations.

title: Nonlocal Cubic Density Gibbs Measures From Bosonic Gibbs States With Three-Body Interactions
authors: Hao Liang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23041v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the high-temperature mean-field limit of grand-canonical bosonic Gibbs states on the torus with renormalized nonlocal three-body interactions. In dimensions two and three, we construct the limiting nonlinear classical Gibbs measure and prove convergence of the relative free energy and of the reduced density matrices of every fixed order; in three dimensions, a smallness condition on the interaction is imposed. The proof combines the density-channel representation of the interaction with a coherent-state variational method based on the upper-symbol representation of the free Gibbs state. The same framework also contains, as a special case, the homogeneous positive-type model studied by Lewin, Nam, and Rougerie (2021).
tldr: This paper studies the high-temperature mean-field limit of bosonic Gibbs states with nonlocal three-body interactions, constructing limiting classical Gibbs measures and proving convergence of free energy and reduced density matrices.
motivation: To understand the behavior of bosonic systems with three-body interactions in the mean-field limit, extending previous work on two-body interactions.
method: Combines the density-channel representation of the interaction with a coherent-state variational method based on the upper-symbol representation of the free Gibbs state.
result: In dimensions two and three, the limiting nonlinear classical Gibbs measure is constructed, and convergence of relative free energy and reduced density matrices is proved, with a smallness condition in three dimensions.
conclusion: The framework provides a rigorous treatment of nonlocal three-body interactions in bosonic Gibbs states, generalizing known results for homogeneous positive-type models.

title: $\mathcal{P}(\Phi)_2$ Theory From Many-body Quantum Gibbs States
authors: Phan Th\`anh Nam, Zhilin Yang, Xiangchan Zhu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive the [MATH] measure on the two-dimensional unit torus as the rigorous limit of many-body quantum Gibbs states. In particular, the quantum model corresponding to the [MATH] measure is formulated in the grand-canonical ensemble with a general symmetric [MATH]-body interaction potential which is not required to have a factorized form. Unlike in the [MATH] case investigated by Fr\"ohlich--Knowles--Schlein--Sohinger in , in the treatment of higher-order interactions, Wick renormalization generates a full hierarchy of lower-order interactions which we organize systematically using a graphical formalism. One key ingredient of our analysis is a logarithmic stability estimate for both the nonlocal Hartree functional and the many-body Hamiltonian that is uniform in the interaction range, allowing us to use the positivity of the leading [MATH]-body interaction to control all lower-order terms generated by the Wick counterterms.
tldr: This paper rigorously derives the P(Phi)_2 Euclidean quantum field theory measure as the limit of many-body quantum Gibbs states with general symmetric interactions.
motivation: To establish a rigorous connection between many-body quantum statistical mechanics and constructive quantum field theory, extending previous work on the Phi^4 model to higher-order interactions.
method: The authors formulate the quantum model in the grand-canonical ensemble with a general symmetric k-body interaction potential, use Wick renormalization to handle divergences, and develop a graphical formalism to organize lower-order counterterms. A logarithmic stability estimate uniform in the interaction range is key.
result: They prove that the grand-canonical Gibbs state converges to the P(Phi)_2 measure on the two-dimensional torus, controlling all lower-order terms generated by Wick renormalization.
conclusion: The work provides a rigorous limit of many-body quantum Gibbs states to a Euclidean quantum field theory, advancing the mathematical foundations of quantum field theory and statistical mechanics.

title: Kinetic And Hydrodynamic Theories Of Chiral Intruder Dynamics In Nonequilibrium Baths
