result: The scheme can sense both alignment and mode mismatch using only QPDs, provides redundancy and increased sensitivity, and works without RF modulation.
conclusion: The technique offers a simple, redundant, and sensitive method for cavity diagnostics, useful in complex optical experiments.

title: An Index To Quantify Scientific Debt
authors: N. Zen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: I propose the index [MATH], defined as [MATH], where [MATH] is the impact factor of the journal in the publication year of the [MATH]-th retracted paper. Whereas the [MATH]-index is a forward-looking measure of scientific achievement, the [MATH]-index quantifies scientific debt. The quantity [MATH] may provide a more balanced assessment of scientific value.
tldr: The paper proposes an index to quantify scientific debt based on retracted papers and journal impact factors.
motivation: To provide a more balanced assessment of scientific value by accounting for retractions.
method: Defines an index using the impact factor of journals at the time of retraction of papers.
result: Introduces a new metric for scientific debt.
conclusion: The index may complement existing measures like the h-index.

title: Investigating Planar Proca Metamaterials In Nonlinear (2+1)-Electrodynamics
authors: Widervan de Deus Morais, Stamatios Strikos, Ronaldo Thibes, Jos\'e Abdalla Helay\"el-Neto
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23013v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The present work pursues the investigation of the physics of a planar electromagnetic system incorporating nonlinear effects, as well as de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass terms in vacuum, which can be tuned to describe new planar metamaterials (MTMs) potentially suitable for technological applications. As a result, we observe interesting effects generated by a spatially dispersive profile that emerges from non-linearity. This characterizes the three-dimensional QED vacuum as a nonlocal metamaterial. The constitutive relations are derived, and the dielectric function of the metamaterial (MTM) exhibits spatial dispersion due to the Chern-Simons mass. The dispersion relations are analyzed in terms of applied external electromagnetic fields and both the de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass parameters. We also notice that, in the special case in which only a background magnetic field is present, this field gives no contribution neither to the dielectric function nor to the spatial dispersion profile, as is the case when both the electric and magnetic fields are present.
tldr: This paper studies nonlinear planar Proca metamaterials with Chern-Simons terms, focusing on electromagnetic properties and dispersion relations.
motivation: To explore the physics of planar electromagnetic systems with nonlinear effects and mass terms, potentially leading to new metamaterials for technological applications.
method: The authors derive constitutive relations and dielectric functions for a planar system incorporating de Broglie-Proca and Chern-Simons mass terms, analyzing dispersion relations under external fields.
result: Spatial dispersion emerges from the Chern-Simons mass; a background magnetic field alone does not affect the dielectric function or dispersion.
conclusion: The system exhibits nonlocal metamaterial behavior, with potential for tunable electromagnetic properties.

title: Explicit Higher Order Rational Rogue Waves Of The Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Equation
authors: Robert Conte, ENS Paris-Saclay, The University Of Hong Kong
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23151v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The [MATH]-th order rational rogue wave of the nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (NLS), which depends on [MATH] real parameters, has been shown to be impossible to generate by the nonlinear superposition formula. We here generate this sequence by a three-term recurrence relation, each step only requiring the computation of three [MATH]-th order determinants of [MATH] variables, while the previous method requires two determinants of order [MATH] in [MATH] variables. This allows us to obtain explicitly the seventh wave with its six arbitrary complex parameters. These very compact expressions open the possibility to investigate the possible existence of new patterns in addition to the already observed ones (concentric rings, polygonal configurations, \dots).
tldr: This paper presents an efficient recurrence method to generate higher-order rational rogue waves of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation.
motivation: Previous methods for generating higher-order rational rogue waves are computationally expensive, requiring large determinants. The authors aim to provide a more efficient recurrence relation.
method: A three-term recurrence relation is derived, requiring only three nth-order determinants of n variables per step, compared to two determinants of order n(n+1)/2 in previous methods.
result: The seventh-order rogue wave with six arbitrary complex parameters is explicitly obtained, and the compact expressions may reveal new patterns.
conclusion: The new recurrence method significantly reduces computational complexity and enables the study of higher-order rogue wave patterns.

title: Non-volatile Integrated Photonics On Lithium Tantalate-on-insulator
authors: Yuhang Li, Miao Deng, Xun Zhang, Cheng Zeng, Chijun Li, Yiqi Dai, Yuankang Huang, Siyu Lu, Zhenwu Mo, Xiao Wu, Peng Tan, Yong Zhang, Yikai Su, Jinsong Xia
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scalable reconfigurable photonic integrated circuits require low-loss, high-speed optical control without continuous holding power. Yet widely used thermo-optic tuning and continuously biased electro-optic tuning consume static power and introduce thermal crosstalk or bias drift. Here we demonstrate a monolithic non-volatile photonics platform on lithium tantalate-on-insulator (LTOI). In congruent x-cut lithium tantalate, the switched ferroelectric-domain configuration is retained after the write field is removed. On the same LTOI platform, we demonstrate a waveguide propagation loss of approximately 0.05-0.06 dB/cm and multilevel non-volatile phase tuning in separate devices. The programmed states remain distinguishable through [MATH] write cycles. Weighted segmented electrodes resolve 137 phase positions across a [MATH] range, corresponding to an analogue phase-setting resolution of approximately [MATH]. We further combine non-volatile phase control with high-speed electro-optic modulation to achieve zero-static-power bias control of a >110 GHz modulator and a 59.3 dB extinction ratio after non-volatile trimming. At the system level, an image-edge-detection chip achieves a measured energy efficiency of 3.48 TOPS/W. These results establish LTOI as an integrated photonics platform that combines persistent optical reconfigurability with low-loss routing and high-speed electro-optic modulation.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a non-volatile integrated photonics platform on lithium tantalate-on-insulator for low-loss, zero-static-power optical reconfiguration and high-speed modulation.
motivation: Scalable reconfigurable photonic integrated circuits require low-loss, high-speed optical control without continuous holding power, but existing thermo-optic and electro-optic tuning consume static power or suffer from drift.
method: The authors fabricate monolithic devices on congruent x-cut lithium tantalate, exploiting ferroelectric domain switching for non-volatile phase tuning, and combine it with high-speed electro-optic modulation.
result: They achieve waveguide loss ~0.05-0.06 dB/cm, multilevel non-volatile phase tuning with 137 phase positions, zero-static-power bias control of a >110 GHz modulator, and an image-edge-detection chip with 3.48 TOPS/W energy efficiency.
conclusion: Lithium tantalate-on-insulator is established as a platform that combines persistent optical reconfigurability with low-loss routing and high-speed modulation, suitable for photonic integrated circuits.

title: Curl-based Electric-Field Boundary Condition For The Accurate And Stable Electromagnetic Scattering Analysis
authors: Eduard Ubeda, Alex Heldring, Juan M. Rius, Vladimir Okhmatovski
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23260v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a curl-based Electric-Field Integral Equation (Curl-EFIE) for the electromagnetic scattering analysis from perfect electric conductors. The formulation is derived by enforcing a vanishing curl on the EFIE over the boundary manifold, achieved by testing the internal electric field with orthogonal tangent solenoidal disks. We demonstrate that a Method-of-Moments (MoM) discretization of the Curl-EFIE converges to a Galerkin-discretized MFIE as the testing disk dimensions vanish, yielding stable, breakdown-free impedance matrices for low frequencies and dense grids. Unlike the strongly singular kernels of the MFIE, the Curl-EFIE utilizes weakly singular kernels, significantly simplifying source integral evaluations. As a first-kind integral equation, it bypasses the MFIE's Gram matrix requirement, facilitating the analysis of non-matching triangulations. Furthermore, a linear combination of the Curl-EFIE and the conventional EFIE provides an interior-resonance-free formulation analogous to the Combined Field Integral Equation (CFIE). Finally, the Curl-EFIE performs particularly well at capturing the scattering behavior of sharp- edged and cornered geometries.
tldr: This paper introduces a curl-based electric-field integral equation for electromagnetic scattering analysis, which is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
motivation: To develop a stable and accurate numerical method for electromagnetic scattering from perfect electric conductors, addressing issues like low-frequency breakdown and interior resonances.
method: Derives a Curl-EFIE by enforcing vanishing curl on the EFIE using orthogonal tangent solenoidal disks, and discretizes it with Method of Moments.
result: The Curl-EFIE converges to a Galerkin-discretized MFIE as testing disks shrink, uses weakly singular kernels, and avoids Gram matrix requirements, enabling analysis of non-matching triangulations and sharp geometries.
conclusion: The Curl-EFIE provides a stable, breakdown-free formulation for electromagnetic scattering, but has no connection to the user's research interests in quantum information theory or related fields.

title: Archetypometrics Of 'Friends'
authors: Shun Zhang, Tabia Tanzin Prama, Christopher M. Danforth, Peter Sheridan Dodds
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23296v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Storytelling inherently revolves around characters. Using the television sitcom `Friends' as a case study, we investigate how well archetype vectors capture both individual characterization and the relational structure of a specific ensemble. Our work is based on the archetypometrics framework, which locates 2,000 fictional characters from 341 stories in a continuous space derived from 464 bipolar traits. We proceed in three stages: interpreting each character's archetypal profile against narrative evidence, projecting the ensemble onto ousiograms of the six essential dimensions, and measuring pairwise similarity with vector inner products. We show that the six characters of `Friends' occupy distinct archetypal positions that accord with their established identities, while the projections expose ensemble structure invisible in individual profiles, including the collapse of the Angel--Demon dimension, a signature of the sitcom's uniformly sympathetic cast. Based on inner products, we construct a similarity matrix that resolves three main kinds of relational structure: alignment (e.g., Phoebe--Joey), contrast (e.g., Phoebe--Ross), and orthogonality (e.g., Rachel--Ross and Monica--Chandler). The orthogonality of the romantic pairings affords a detailed view of relationships built on complementary rather than overlapping character traits. Overall, our case study suggests that for ensemble-based stories the archetypometric geometry is fully interpretable in narrative terms, from individual identities to the structure of the group's relationships.
tldr: This paper applies archetypometric analysis to the TV show 'Friends', mapping characters onto bipolar trait dimensions and examining relational structures.
motivation: To demonstrate how archetype vectors can capture individual characterization and relational structure in ensemble stories.
method: Using a pre-existing archetypometrics framework with 464 bipolar traits, the authors interpret character profiles, project onto six essential dimensions, and compute pairwise similarity via inner products.
result: The six characters occupy distinct archetypal positions; the Angel-Demon dimension collapses, indicating uniformly sympathetic characters; similarity matrix reveals alignment, contrast, and orthogonality relationships.
conclusion: Archetypometric geometry is fully interpretable for ensemble-based stories, from individual identities to group relationship structure.

title: Pi-ginot: Data-free Geometry-informed Neural Operator Learning For Finite-strain Hyperelasticity On Parametric DogBone Specimens
authors: Betim Bahtiri Aamir Dean
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Parametric nonlinear solid-mechanics simulations are widely used in virtual testing, optimisation, and uncertainty analysis, but repeated finite-element simulations become costly when geometry changes. This paper presents PI-GINOT, a physics-informed neural operator that predicts finite-strain hyperelastic responses across a four-parameter family of DogBone specimens without using finite-element training data. Each specimen is described by a boundary point cloud, which is encoded into geometry features. A cross-attention decoder then predicts displacement at arbitrary points. Displacement boundary conditions are enforced exactly, while stresses are computed using automatic differentiation and a compressible Neo-Hookean plane-stress model. Training is guided by equilibrium, traction-free and symmetry conditions, deformation stability, and internal force consistency. Abaqus simulations are used only after training for validation. Across eight test geometries, PI-GINOT achieves displacement errors of 2.1%-7.1%, peak von Mises stress errors of 0.9%-13.3%, and section-force errors below 10.3%. Larger errors occur in individual stress components, especially for narrow specimens, mainly because of steep stress gradients near the gauge-to-fillet transition. These results show that PI-GINOT can provide useful geometry-dependent predictions for nonlinear solid mechanics without labelled simulation data, while also revealing where better local stress resolution is still needed.
tldr: This paper presents a physics-informed neural operator for finite-strain hyperelasticity on parametric DogBone specimens without using finite-element training data.
motivation: Parametric nonlinear solid-mechanics simulations are costly when geometry changes, motivating a data-free neural operator approach.
method: PI-GINOT encodes boundary point clouds into geometry features and uses a cross-attention decoder to predict displacements, with training guided by equilibrium, traction-free, symmetry, and stability conditions.
result: Across eight test geometries, displacement errors are 2.1%-7.1%, peak von Mises stress errors 0.9%-13.3%, and section-force errors below 10.3%.
conclusion: PI-GINOT provides useful geometry-dependent predictions for nonlinear solid mechanics without labelled data, but stress resolution near steep gradients needs improvement.

title: Self-consistent Orbital-free Nuclear Density Functional Theory With A Physics-constrained Learned Nonlocal Kinetic Energy Functional
authors: Fumihiro Imoto
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23328v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Nonlocal kinetic-energy density functionals (KEDFs) can encode nuclear shell structure in orbital-free density functional theory (OFDFT), but self-consistency requires accurate functional derivatives and a stable solution of the Euler equation. We construct a density-dependent-kernel KEDF whose correction is learned from Kohn-Sham (KS) reference data. Linearity in the kernel shape yields analytic Euler--Lagrange (EL) responses. The fit uses exact energy-matching equalities and soft quadratic inequality penalties for violations of prescribed tail-response and selected-path energy-rise margins, evaluated by an active-set repeated penalized least-squares iteration. We formulate the radial EL equation as the rearranged one-orbital eigenproblem. In a constant-[MATH] [MATH]O benchmark it converges without density mixing and agrees with imaginary-time evolution (ITE) to sub-keV energy. Adaptive-step ITE gives final species EL residuals of at most 0.07 MeV in the reported calculations, and rearranged diagonalization reaches the same stationary densities. For spherical [MATH] systems without spin--orbit or Coulomb terms, nucleus-specific fits for [MATH] to [MATH] reproduce shell patterns and radii. A correction trained on three nuclei transfers the shell pattern and radius, but not the absolute energy, to a previously unseen [MATH] system.
tldr: This paper presents a machine learning approach to construct a nonlocal kinetic energy density functional for orbital-free density functional theory, applied to nuclear structure calculations.
motivation: Orbital-free DFT is computationally efficient but lacks accurate kinetic energy functionals that capture nuclear shell structure; the authors aim to learn a correction from Kohn-Sham data while ensuring self-consistency.
method: A density-dependent kernel KEDF is constructed with linearity in kernel shape for analytic Euler-Lagrange responses, trained via active-set repeated penalized least-squares using exact energy-matching equalities and soft penalties for constraint violations.
result: The method converges without density mixing in a constant-potential benchmark, reproduces shell patterns and radii for spherical nuclei, and transfers shell structure to an unseen nucleus.
conclusion: The learned nonlocal KEDF enables self-consistent OFDFT with nuclear shell effects, but the approach is specific to nuclear physics and does not connect to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Optimal Investment With Switching Preferences
authors: Yu-Jui Huang, Liviu Ignat, Traian A. Pirvu, Reihaneh Vafadar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Major life events can significantly increase individuals' risk aversion over a sustained period of time, as empirical studies reveal. How such an event-triggered shift of risk preferences impacts optimal investment is the focus of this paper. On a finite time horizon where a major life event may occur independently of the financial market, an investor aims to maximize her expected utility from terminal wealth while foreseeing a potential change in her risk aversion. We find that the associated Hamilton--Jacobi--Bellman (HJB) equation involves the post-event optimal value function (under elevated but fixed risk aversion after the event's occurrence), and the Fenchel--Legendre transform fails to linearize this HJB equation: it yields a parabolic equation with a fully nonlinear term, induced precisely by the post-event optimal value function. Through a combination of fixed-point, compactness, and verification arguments, we establish the existence of a positive convex classical solution with suitable growth to the fully-nonlinear parabolic equation. The convex conjugate of this solution is shown to satisfy the HJB equation and coincides with the pre-event optimal value function. The optimal trading strategy is obtained by concatenating the optimal pre-event and post-event strategies -- the former is expressed in terms of the solution to the HJB equation and the latter is traditional Merton's ratio.
tldr: This paper studies optimal investment strategies when an investor's risk aversion may increase due to a major life event, using stochastic control and PDE methods.
motivation: Empirical studies show that major life events can increase risk aversion over sustained periods, but the impact on optimal investment is not well understood.
method: The authors formulate a finite-horizon utility maximization problem with a potential shift in risk aversion, derive a fully nonlinear HJB equation involving the post-event value function, and prove existence of a classical solution via fixed-point and verification arguments.
result: The optimal strategy concatenates the pre-event strategy (expressed via the HJB solution) and the post-event Merton ratio; the HJB equation is solved by the convex conjugate of the solution to a fully nonlinear parabolic PDE.
conclusion: The paper provides a rigorous framework for optimal investment under event-triggered preference changes, extending classical Merton's problem.

title: A Uniqueness Result For Finite-state Mean Field Games With Non-separable Hamiltonian
authors: Alekos Cecchin, Luca Di Persio, Nicola Fraccarolo
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22537v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a class of continuous-time mean field games on a finite state space with transition rates depending on the population distribution, leading to a non-separable Hamiltonian. In this setting, classical Lasry--Lions monotonicity arguments do not apply directly. We establish a new uniqueness result on arbitrary time horizons under a combination of strong monotonicity assumptions on the costs and quantitative bounds on the interaction term in the dynamics.
tldr: This paper proves a uniqueness result for finite-state mean field games with non-separable Hamiltonian.
motivation: Mean field games with non-separable Hamiltonians are challenging because classical monotonicity arguments fail; a uniqueness result is needed to ensure well-posedness.
method: The authors impose strong monotonicity assumptions on costs and quantitative bounds on the interaction term in the dynamics, then use a fixed-point argument to prove uniqueness.
result: Uniqueness of the solution is established on arbitrary time horizons under the given assumptions.
conclusion: The result provides a theoretical foundation for analyzing mean field games with non-separable Hamiltonians, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Low-Rank Kkt Updates And A Parallel Flipping Mechanism For Model-Based Derivative-Free Optimization
authors: Pengcheng Xie Donghan Wu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22538v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Model-based derivative-free optimization relies on quadratic interpolation, but maintaining these models typically requires [MATH] linear system solves. We show that for the least Frobenius norm updating model, the associated KKT matrix possesses a fixed inner-product structure. Both single-point replacements and a proposed coordinate-axis flipping operation induce exact Rank-2 perturbations to this matrix. Using this structure, we derive an [MATH] update formula for the KKT inverse, eliminating costly refactorizations at each iteration. We integrate the update into a parallel trust-region algorithm where workers independently flip interpolation axes, refresh local models, and synchronize the best configuration. Tests on 530 benchmark problems show the method reduces model-maintenance overhead and achieves higher success rates under tight function-evaluation budgets compared to standard solvers.
tldr: This paper presents a low-rank update method for KKT matrices in model-based derivative-free optimization, with a parallel flipping mechanism.
motivation: Model-based derivative-free optimization requires costly linear system solves for model maintenance; the authors aim to reduce this overhead.
method: They exploit a fixed inner-product structure in the KKT matrix to derive exact Rank-2 updates for single-point replacements and coordinate-axis flipping, and integrate this into a parallel trust-region algorithm.
result: Tests on 530 benchmark problems show reduced model-maintenance overhead and higher success rates under tight function-evaluation budgets compared to standard solvers.
conclusion: The proposed method improves efficiency and success rates in derivative-free optimization.

title: Comparing Optimization Models For Radiotherapy Scheduling
authors: C. C. Rambaldi Migliore, D. Stanicel, N. Musliu, G. Iacca, M. Roveri
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Radiotherapy Scheduling Problem (RTSP) involves determining an optimal schedule for patients undergoing radiation treatments, a task that has a massive impact on clinical outcomes given the central role of radiotherapy in cancer care. The daily batch approach--which consists of scheduling all the newly arrived patients together at the end of each day--modelled with Integer Linear Programming, is currently one of the most effective methods for the RTSP. However, this kind of formulation requires substantial computational resources in terms of time and memory. Here, we address these limitations by developing two novel greedy heuristics (named RTSP First Fit and RTSP Best Fit) and use them as constructive heuristics for a Simulated Annealing (SA) approach to optimize the scheduling. The proposed methods--the heuristics alone and their combination with SA--are evaluated on a publicly available dataset against an integer linear program formulation solved with two different state-of-the-art exact solvers. Evaluation metrics include six scheduling objectives capturing patient waiting times, preference satisfaction, and changes in linear accelerator assignment (aggregated in four different weight configurations), solving time, and memory consumption. The results show that the novel heuristics achieve solutions close to those of exact methods, while dramatically reducing runtime and memory usage; furthermore, when combined with SA, they further improve the solution quality while maintaining low runtime and memory usage.
tldr: This paper proposes greedy heuristics and simulated annealing for radiotherapy scheduling, an operations research problem with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Radiotherapy scheduling is important for clinical outcomes but exact methods are computationally expensive.
method: Two greedy heuristics (First Fit, Best Fit) are developed and used as constructive heuristics for Simulated Annealing; compared against Integer Linear Programming with exact solvers.
result: The heuristics achieve near-optimal solutions with dramatically reduced runtime and memory usage; SA further improves quality.
conclusion: The proposed methods are efficient alternatives for radiotherapy scheduling, but the work is unrelated to the user's research interests.

title: Sde Guided Monte Carlo Reinforcement Learning: A Stochastic Maximum Principle Approach For Robust Decision Making In Noisy Environments
authors: Juncai Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22541v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This work investigates whether the qualitative optimality conditions of the SMP can serve as guiding heuristics for designing robust tabular RL algorithms. We propose the framework, which establishes a set of SMP-inspired correspondences: the potential field gradient is mapped to potential-based reward shaping, the diffusion coefficient to a softmax temperature, and the value function gradient magnitude to the episode-averaged absolute temporal-difference (TD) error. Crucially, we derive an SMP-motivated adaptive temperature schedule that scales exploration stochastically in response to local value uncertainty. The resulting Monte Carlo Actor-Critic agent integrates potential-shaped rewards, entropy regularization, and adaptive temperature control within episodic updates. We conduct a set of five principled experiments in a minimal, fixed maze testbed under three canonical noise regimes (perceptual, dynamic goal, action) to test five falsifiable hypotheses derived from the SMP. Our results provide evidence for (i) an inverted-U optimal stochasticity curve, (ii) the robust failure prevention of the adaptive schedule under non-stationary noise, (iii) convergence acceleration by potential field guidance, (iv) cross-noise generalization, and (v) the indispensability of the combined SDE components through systematic ablation. Trajectory visualizations reveal a characteristic ``macroscopically deterministic, microscopically stochastic'' navigation pattern consistent with the SDE model. The study demonstrates that even a heuristic transposition of the SMP into a discrete MDP can yield significant empirical gains, thereby opening a bridge between rigorous stochastic optimal control and practical robust reinforcement learning.
tldr: This paper applies stochastic maximum principle to Monte Carlo reinforcement learning for robust decision making in noisy environments.
motivation: To bridge stochastic optimal control and robust reinforcement learning by using SMP as guiding heuristics.
method: Proposes an SMP-inspired framework mapping potential field gradient to reward shaping, diffusion coefficient to softmax temperature, and value function gradient to TD error, with an adaptive temperature schedule.
result: Experiments in a maze testbed under three noise regimes show an inverted-U optimal stochasticity curve, robust failure prevention, convergence acceleration, cross-noise generalization, and indispensability of combined SDE components.
conclusion: Heuristic transposition of SMP into discrete MDP yields significant empirical gains, opening a bridge between stochastic optimal control and robust RL.

title: A Hybrid Matheuristic Framework For The Chinese Postman Problem With Load-Dependent Costs
authors: Thieu Khang Nguyen, Thu Huong Dang, Truong-Son Hy
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22542v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Chinese Postman Problem with load-dependent costs (CPP-LC) arises in real-world logistics and transportation systems where travel costs depend on vehicle load and energy consumption. In this work, we propose a hybrid optimization framework that integrates metaheuristic search with mathematical programming to efficiently solve CPP-LC. The proposed method combines local search procedures with reduced mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) models to balance exploration and intensification. In addition, we develop an Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm to enhance scalability on large instances. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently achieves high-quality solutions and outperforms existing approaches in solution quality, while maintaining competitive computational efficiency. These results highlight the effectiveness of hybrid optimization strategies for complex, load-dependent routing problems in practical applications. Our implementation is publicly available at [URL].
tldr: This paper proposes a hybrid optimization framework for the Chinese Postman Problem with load-dependent costs, combining metaheuristic search and mathematical programming.
motivation: Real-world logistics and transportation systems require efficient solutions for routing problems where travel costs depend on vehicle load and energy consumption.
method: The framework integrates local search procedures with reduced mixed-integer linear programming models and an Ant Colony Optimization algorithm to balance exploration and intensification.
result: Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets show that the proposed framework consistently achieves high-quality solutions and outperforms existing approaches in solution quality while maintaining competitive computational efficiency.
conclusion: Hybrid optimization strategies are effective for complex, load-dependent routing problems in practical applications.

title: Route Based Map Matching Via A Structured Codebook And Token Sequence Decoding
authors: Takara Sakai
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22543v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study proposes an efficient and computationally light route based map matching method for GPS track data on urban expressway networks. The key idea is to exploit a symbolic structure of named lines and named junctions that link level map matching leaves unused. We represent each candidate route as a sequence of line and junction names, take the set of such sequences as a route codebook, and formulate map matching as scored alignment of a probe trajectory against members of the codebook. Probes become token sequences via a mesh quantizer, a precomputed grid mapping each coordinate to a line or junction token, and the decoder returns a member of the codebook by construction. The codebook is indexed by a DAFSA [MATH] Levenshtein automaton, a fuzzy lookup technique from approximate string matching and speech recognition; the per query decoding cost is orders of magnitude lower than a brute force scan. We evaluate the method on a deformed replica of the Tokyo Metropolitan Expressway topology. The method recovers the exact route at moderate GPS noise and continues to identify the line and junction sequence under heavy noise; a sensitivity analysis maps the mesh resolution operating range. Real probe evaluation, channel model calibration, and a head to head HMM comparison are left to a forthcoming version.
tldr: This paper proposes a route-based map matching method for GPS data using a structured codebook and token sequence decoding, applied to urban expressway networks.
motivation: Existing map matching methods are computationally heavy; the authors aim to exploit symbolic route structures (line and junction names) for efficiency.
method: Candidate routes are represented as token sequences (line/junction names) forming a codebook; probe GPS points are quantized into tokens via a mesh grid, and matching is performed using a DAFSA-based Levenshtein automaton for fast fuzzy lookup.
result: The method recovers exact routes under moderate GPS noise and identifies line/junction sequences under heavy noise, with per-query cost orders of magnitude lower than brute force.
conclusion: The approach is efficient and robust for urban expressway networks, though real-world evaluation and comparison to HMM are left for future work.

title: Bayesian Fuzzy Optimization Using Fuzzy Gaussian Process
authors: Sourav Das, Debdas Ghosh, Debjani Chakraborty, Pabitra Mitra
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In many real-life problems, decision-making gets complicated due to dual sources of uncertainty, known as randomness and fuzziness or imprecision, which can be challenging for traditional optimization methods. Most of the existing fuzzy optimization techniques that optimize fuzzy-valued objective functions ignore fuzziness, while the probabilistic optimization techniques ignore randomness. To handle this dual source of uncertainty, Kwakernaak introduced the concept of a fuzzy random variable as ``random variables whose values are not real, but fuzzy numbers". This work aims to derive a theoretical background for the Gaussian fuzzy process and fuzzy acquisition functions, which will be used to develop a novel (BFO) technique that optimizes a fuzzy-values objective function. Based on fuzzy random variables, the Gaussian fuzzy process is developed, which is used as a prior belief about the fuzzy-valued objective function in the BFO. Fuzzy acquisition functions are defined to act as a guide for the search process of BFO with the help of posterior fuzzy mean and fuzzy variance. The proposed method demonstrated effective performance in both fuzzy mean-variance portfolio allocation and Indian temperature data analysis, showing robust predictive accuracy and adaptability. The proposed method can have broader applications in various fields like healthcare, material science, agriculture, etc.
tldr: This paper proposes a Bayesian fuzzy optimization method using a fuzzy Gaussian process to handle dual uncertainty from randomness and fuzziness.
motivation: Real-life optimization problems often involve both randomness and fuzziness, which traditional methods fail to address simultaneously.
method: The authors develop a Gaussian fuzzy process based on fuzzy random variables and define fuzzy acquisition functions to guide the optimization search.
result: The method shows effective performance in fuzzy mean-variance portfolio allocation and Indian temperature data analysis.
conclusion: The proposed Bayesian fuzzy optimization technique can handle dual uncertainty and has potential applications in various fields.

title: Learning To Optimize At Scale: A Benders Decomposition-TransfORmers Framework For Stochastic Combinatorial Optimization
authors: Seung Jin Choi, Kimiya Jozani, Josh Cooper, Esra Buyuktahtakin Toy
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22550v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose a learning-augmented Benders decomposition framework to solve large-scale two-stage stochastic mixed-integer programs. We focus on the two-stage stochastic capacitated lot-sizing problem (TSSCLSP) under demand uncertainty. Our method accelerates the convergence of the decomposition by using a pre-trained TransfORmer model to rapidly generate high-quality approximate solutions for the scenario subproblems. This hybrid strategy uses the TransfORmer predictions to generate strong optimality and feasibility cuts, effectively guiding the Benders master problem. Our framework includes a novel expandable generation mechanism, allowing a model trained on a fixed horizon to solve instances of arbitrary length. For the test set considered, our method solves instances up to T = 270, a scale previously intractable for this approach, while maintaining zero infeasibility in the generated subproblem solutions. This demonstrates the potential of TransfORmers as powerful surrogate solvers embedded within classical decomposition algorithms.
tldr: This paper proposes a learning-augmented Benders decomposition framework for stochastic combinatorial optimization, specifically for lot-sizing problems.
motivation: Large-scale stochastic mixed-integer programs are computationally challenging; traditional decomposition methods converge slowly.
method: A pre-trained Transformer model generates approximate solutions for scenario subproblems, which are used to produce strong optimality and feasibility cuts within a Benders decomposition framework.
result: The method solves instances up to T=270, a scale previously intractable, with zero infeasibility in subproblem solutions.
conclusion: Transformers can serve as effective surrogate solvers embedded in classical decomposition algorithms for stochastic optimization.

title: Mirror Descent Methods For Quasar Convex Optimization Problems With Non-Smooth Inequality Constraints
authors: Mohammad Alkousa
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we consider constraint optimization problems subject to non-smooth convex functional (inequality-type) constraints, wherein the objective function is non-smooth and quasar convex. We propose and analyze two groups of algorithms, each consisting of a standard version and a modified variant, that operate by switching between two types of iteration points: productive and non-productive. Within each group, we develop distinct mirror descent-type algorithms for both deterministic and stochastic settings, and we establish their convergence rates.
tldr: This paper proposes mirror descent methods for quasar convex optimization with non-smooth inequality constraints.
motivation: The paper addresses constrained optimization problems where the objective is quasar convex, a generalization of convexity, and constraints are non-smooth.
method: Two groups of mirror descent algorithms (standard and modified) are developed for deterministic and stochastic settings, switching between productive and non-productive iteration points.
result: Convergence rates are established for the proposed algorithms.
conclusion: The algorithms provide efficient solutions for quasar convex optimization with inequality constraints.

title: Major-Minor Lq Mean Field Games With Erroneous Initial Information: Distributed Error Estimation And Strategy Modification
authors: Yuxin Jin, Haotian Wang, Wang Yao, Xiao Zhang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22558v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies major-minor linear-quadratic mean field games (MMLQMFGs) with erroneous initial information under a constrained observation structure. Each minor agent observes only its own state and the major agent's state, while the major agent observes its own state and the states of a subset of minor agents; neither side observes the mean field state directly. We show that the initial-information errors propagate linearly through the game dynamics and lead to explicit deviations in the major state, the actual mean field, and the agents' internally updated mean field states. Based on this structure, we formulate distributed error identification as a parameter-estimation problem from discrete-time local observations and construct maximum-likelihood estimators for unknown initial errors. We then propose an estimate-based strategy modification at an intermediate time by reconstructing the current mean field from the estimated errors and switching to the corresponding control law. We also characterize the resulting estimation errors and show that, in the present symmetric setting, the major agent's estimation precision depends on the number of observed minor agents but not on their identities. Numerical results illustrate the proposed method.
tldr: This paper studies major-minor linear-quadratic mean field games with erroneous initial information and proposes distributed error estimation and strategy modification.
motivation: To address the challenge of initial information errors in mean field games with constrained observations, which can lead to suboptimal strategies.
method: Formulates error identification as a parameter-estimation problem using maximum-likelihood estimators from local observations, then modifies strategies at an intermediate time based on estimated errors.
result: Shows that initial errors propagate linearly and that the major agent's estimation precision depends on the number of observed minor agents but not their identities.
conclusion: The proposed method effectively estimates and corrects initial errors, improving strategy performance in mean field games.

title: Granular Fractional Caputo-Katugampola Derivatives And Their Applications In Optimality Conditions For Fuzzy Fractional Variational Problems
authors: Le Thanh Tung, Tran Thien Khai, Pham Le Bach Ngoc, Trinh Tung
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this article, we present the new definition of the fuzzy Caputo-Katugampola derivative and its related concepts for the class of fuzzy functions and apply them to establish both necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for fractional fuzzy variational problems. By adopting the horizontal membership functional representation of fuzzy numbers, the granular Caputo-Katugampola derivatives offer higher computational efficiency than the previous approaches in certain scenarios. The optimality conditions for the fuzzy fractional variational problems under granular fuzzy Caputo fractional derivatives are also examined and illustrated with detailed examples. Another novel aspect of our results, even in the non-fuzzy case, is the application of special functions to represent the exact solutions of the fuzzy fractional variational problems.
tldr: This paper introduces granular Caputo-Katugampola fractional derivatives for fuzzy functions and applies them to derive optimality conditions for fuzzy fractional variational problems.
motivation: To extend fractional calculus to fuzzy functions and provide efficient computational methods for solving fuzzy variational problems.
method: Defines fuzzy Caputo-Katugampola derivatives using horizontal membership functional representation, then derives necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for fuzzy fractional variational problems.
result: New optimality conditions are established and illustrated with examples; special functions are used to represent exact solutions even in non-fuzzy cases.
conclusion: The proposed granular approach offers higher computational efficiency and provides a framework for solving fuzzy fractional variational problems.

title: Efficient Multidisciplinary Design Via Bayesian Optimization
authors: Nathalie Bartoli, Thierry Lefebvre, R\'emi Lafage, Paul Saves, Youssef Diouane, Joseph Morlier
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22560v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study introduces SEGOMOE, a Bayesian optimization tool for optimizing complex, computationally expensive systems, especially in aeronautics. It efficiently handles mixed design variables (continuous, discrete, categorical, hierarchical) using adaptive Gaussian process models. SEGOMOE combines expert models to address nonlinearities in objectives and constraints, leveraging the open-source Surrogate Modeling Toolbox (SMT). The tool supports multi-fidelity data and solves both single- and multi-objective problems, including hidden constraints and high-dimensional decomposition. Validated through benchmarks and real-world aeronautical applications, SEGOMOE proves to be robust and versatile for tackling multidisciplinary challenges.
tldr: This paper presents a Bayesian optimization tool for multidisciplinary design in aeronautics, with no connection to quantum information theory or quantum thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to optimize complex, computationally expensive engineering systems, particularly in aeronautics, using Bayesian optimization.
method: The authors introduce SEGOMOE, which uses adaptive Gaussian process models and combines expert models to handle mixed design variables, multi-fidelity data, and multi-objective problems.
result: The tool is validated through benchmarks and real-world aeronautical applications, demonstrating robustness and versatility.
conclusion: SEGOMOE is an effective Bayesian optimization tool for multidisciplinary design challenges, but it is unrelated to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: A Unified Approach To Non-unique Fixed Points Via Modified C-class Ciric-type Contractions
authors: Olaoluwa Omidire, Memudu Olatinwo, Kamiludeen Tijani, Babatunde Ishola
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fixed point theory is central to nonlinear analysis, yet classical results often assume strict contractivity and guarantee uniqueness, limiting applicability to mappings with inherently non-unique fixed points. This paper addresses this gap by introducing a modified C-class function and establishing new non-unique fixed point theorems for Ciric-type mappings in complete metric spaces. We construct a generalized contractive inequality using a three-variable modifed C-class function combined with an altering distance function. Under orbital continuity and orbital completeness, we prove that Picard iteration converges to a fixed point without requiring global Lipschitz conditions or strict contractivity. Carefully designed examples illustrate the sharpness and generality of the framework, strictly extending classical Ciric and Chatterjea contractions as well as hybrid [MATH]-contractions. Our main contributions are: (i) a unified framework encompassing classical and generalized C-class contractions, (ii) existence results for non-unique fixed points, (iii) a simple criterion for uniqueness when desired, and (iv) practical validation through nontrivial examples. These results provide a robust foundation for further research in nonlinear operator theory, iterative methods, and applications in optimization and variational problems.
tldr: This paper introduces a modified C-class function and proves non-unique fixed point theorems for Ciric-type contractions in complete metric spaces.
motivation: Classical fixed point theorems often assume strict contractivity and guarantee uniqueness, limiting applicability to mappings with inherently non-unique fixed points.
method: A generalized contractive inequality is constructed using a three-variable modified C-class function combined with an altering distance function; Picard iteration is shown to converge under orbital continuity and orbital completeness.
result: New non-unique fixed point theorems are established, extending classical Ciric and Chatterjea contractions as well as hybrid contractions, with examples demonstrating generality.
conclusion: The framework provides a unified approach to non-unique fixed points and a foundation for further research in nonlinear operator theory and iterative methods.

title: Optimality Of A Threshold Policy For A Queueing System With One Fast Server And Two Identical Slow Servers
authors: Weina Wang, Taha Ameen, Yudong Chen, Yige Hong, Josh Nichols, Matthew Zurek
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the optimal control problem of a queueing system with three servers: one fast server and two identical slow servers. The two-server version of this problem, with one fast server and one slow server, was introduced by Lin and Kumar (1984), and the optimal policy has been shown to be of threshold type. However, generalizing this result beyond the two-server setting has been considered an open problem. In this paper, we resolve the first nontrivial case by proving that a threshold policy is optimal for the three-server system considered. The core technical ideas in this paper are generated by GPT-5.5 Pro. We have included a short report describing the authors' interactions with GPT-5.5 Pro. The authors verified the proofs and rewrote the paper for better rigor, clarity, and exposition. In addition, three key lemmas have also been verified in Lean 4.
tldr: This paper proves optimality of a threshold policy for a queueing system with one fast and two slow servers, using AI-generated proofs.
motivation: Generalizing the optimal control of two-server queueing systems to three servers has been an open problem.
method: The authors use dynamic programming and structural properties of the value function, with proofs assisted by GPT-5.5 Pro and verified in Lean 4.
result: A threshold policy is proven optimal for the three-server system.
conclusion: The result resolves a nontrivial case of a long-standing open problem in queueing theory.

title: Randomized Constructive Heuristics For The Vrptw: A Focus On Regret-k
authors: Florian Rascoussier (IMT Atlantique - DSD, CITI, Lab-Sticc, EMERAUDE), Romain Billot (IMT Atlantique - DSD, Lab-Sticc, Lab-Sticc\_decide), Lina Fahed (IMT Atlantique - DSD, Lab-Sticc\_decide, Lab-Sticc), Christine Solnon
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTW) requires a fleet of capacitated vehicles to serve customers within strict time windows while minimizing total travel time. Constructive heuristics are fundamental for generating solutions and commonly serve as starting points for metaheuristics such as Iterated Local Search (ILS), Genetic Algorithms, and Ant Colony Optimization (ACO). This work studies three classical constructive heuristics - Nearest Neighbor, Best Insertion, and Regret-k - within a randomized, multi-start framework, a setting that remains largely under-explored despite their well-established deterministic use. We address how to effectively randomize these heuristics and, in particular, propose a novel randomization of Regret-k by separating the ''who'' (which customer to insert next) and ''where'' (insertion position) decisions, applying a probabilistic selection proportional to the regret value to preserve the heuristic's foresight while injecting the diversity needed for a multi-start approach. We further study the impact of combining these greedy randomized constructions with Local Search and ACO. Experiments follow the DIMACS 2021 conventions (integer, truncated Euclidean distances) on the Solomon and Gehring \& Homberger benchmarks (100--1000 customers), comparing against the Best-Known Solutions and the state-of-the-art Hybrid Genetic Search solver, with all critical components implemented in modern C++ and bound to Python via pybind11. To the best of our knowledge, the randomization of Regret-k has never been examined; our analysis highlights the trade-off between solution quality and computational cost, providing a preliminary step toward hybrid methods (ACO, ILS, Branch-and-Price) for the Time-Dependent VRPTW within the MAMUT project.
tldr: This paper studies randomized constructive heuristics for the Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows, a classical combinatorial optimization problem.
motivation: Constructive heuristics are fundamental for generating initial solutions in metaheuristics, but their randomized variants are under-explored.
method: The authors propose a novel randomization of Regret-k by separating customer selection and insertion position decisions, and evaluate it within a multi-start framework combined with local search and ACO.
result: Experiments on standard benchmarks show trade-offs between solution quality and computational cost, with the randomized Regret-k providing diversity.
conclusion: The work provides a preliminary step toward hybrid methods for time-dependent VRPTW, but is purely classical optimization with no quantum or thermodynamic content.

title: Branch \& Price \& Cut For The Time-Dependent Vehicle Routing Problem With Time Windows (tdvrptw)
authors: Florian Rascoussier (IMT Atlantique - DSD, CITI, Lab-Sticc, Lab-Sticc\_decide), Romain Billot (IMT Atlantique - DSD, Lab-Sticc, Lab-Sticc\_decide), Lina Fahed (IMT Atlantique - DSD, Lab-Sticc\_decide), Christine Solnon
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In urban contexts, travel times vary strongly with the time of day and traffic conditions. The Time-Dependent Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (TDVRPTW) extends the classical VRPTW by making travel times depend on departure time, with the objective of minimizing the total travel time of at most [MATH] vehicle routes serving customers within strict time windows. Exact resolution of this realistic yet understudied problem currently relies on the Branch \& Price approach of Dabia et al. (2013), in which a Column Generation scheme decomposes the problem into a set-partitioning master problem and a resource-constrained shortest-path pricing problem solved by dynamic programming. This work, conducted within the MAMUT project (Machine Learning and Matheuristics for Urban Transport), aims to advance the state of the art for the exact and explainable resolution of the TDVRPTW. We propose to reimplement and revisit the pioneering Branch \& Price algorithm by transferring recent advances made on the single-vehicle variant (TDTSPTW) to the multi-vehicle setting, notably an exact anytime extension of A* and a Large Neighborhood Search guided by dynamic programming for the pricing sub-problem. We further explore the integration of data mining and machine learning to guide column generation by exploiting knowledge from previously computed routes. The goal is a high-performance and interpretable solver that meets the requirements of real-world urban transport while preserving guarantees on solution quality.
tldr: This paper presents an exact algorithm for the time-dependent vehicle routing problem with time windows, a combinatorial optimization problem in urban transport.
motivation: Travel times vary with time of day in urban contexts, and exact resolution of the TDVRPTW is understudied yet important for real-world logistics.
method: The authors reimplement and extend a Branch & Price & Cut algorithm, transferring advances from the single-vehicle variant and integrating machine learning to guide column generation.
result: The proposed solver aims to achieve high performance and interpretability while preserving solution quality guarantees.
conclusion: The work advances exact and explainable resolution of TDVRPTW, but is unrelated to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Diamond Transports In Quadratic-form And Distorted Optimal Transport
authors: Zhenyuan Zhang Ruodu Wang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The diamond transport is generated by the uniform law on a diamond-shaped copula support. Since a classical optimal transport (OT) objective is affine in the coupling, this transport cannot be the unique minimizer in the classical setting. We study a broader family of transports, called diamond-type transports, in non-classical settings such as quadratic-form optimal transport (QOT) and distorted optimal transport (DOT), which are generally nonconvex. Our main results are within the QOT framework: for symmetric one-dimensional marginals, the diamond transport is an optimizer for a large class of QOT problems whose costs depend on within-coordinate distances. Examples include product costs under positive-definiteness and convexity conditions and, in particular, mixed rectangular costs. For rectangular costs, we show that the diamond transport is the unique minimizer except for boundary cases. In the DOT framework, diamond-type transports are minimizers for a natural class of cost, and the diamond transport is the unique minimizer in specialized examples. We also identify the intersection between DOT and QOT, which corresponds precisely to quadratic distortion functions.
tldr: This paper studies diamond-type transports in quadratic-form and distorted optimal transport, which are topics in mathematical optimal transport theory with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper aims to characterize optimizers for non-classical optimal transport problems where the classical diamond transport is not unique.
method: The authors analyze quadratic-form optimal transport (QOT) and distorted optimal transport (DOT) frameworks, proving conditions under which diamond-type transports are minimizers.
result: For symmetric one-dimensional marginals, the diamond transport is an optimizer for a large class of QOT problems; for rectangular costs, it is unique except boundary cases. In DOT, diamond-type transports are minimizers for a natural cost class.
conclusion: The work extends optimal transport theory to nonconvex settings but has no relevance to quantum information, thermodynamics, quantum networks, or hybrid quantum systems.

title: Drp-flr: Data-Driven Assessment Of Demand Response Potential For Flexible Load Regulation In Smart Grids
authors: Yunhao Yao, Siyu Jing, Yang Yang, Qiang Xu, Changqi Weng, Xiang-Yang Li
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid growth of AI workloads and renewable energy resources exacerbates supply-demand imbalance in power systems, making traditional load regulation designed for efficient allocation inadequate and motivating demand response (DR) mechanisms to enable load controllability in smart grids. However, existing DR-oriented approaches either focus on optimizing electricity cost or occupant comfort with limited benefit to system-level balance. Others overlook the diverse and dynamic consumption patterns of heterogeneous energy entities, leading to significant over- or under-regulation. Therefore, we propose DRP-FLR. First, DRP-FLR achieves accurate short-term load forecasting by embedding exogenous knowledge (e.g., entity information, prediction time) into historical load representations. Next, it constructs entity-specific load-pattern profiles by clustering historical load curves, and estimates DR potential by matching forecasted loads with pattern profiles. Finally, DRP-FLR formulates flexible load regulation as a mixed-integer optimization problem and solves it with an MILP solver to jointly optimize DR utilization, participant economic benefit, and renewable accommodation, while enforcing supply-demand balance and economic feasibility. Experiments on a regional grid and a campus microgrid show that DRP-FLR reduces regulation deviation by 36.63%-91.87% and improves participant benefit by 44.66% on average.
tldr: This paper proposes a data-driven framework for demand response in smart grids to balance supply and demand using load forecasting and optimization.
motivation: The rapid growth of AI workloads and renewable energy causes supply-demand imbalance, and existing demand response methods either optimize cost/comfort without system-level balance or ignore diverse consumption patterns.
method: DRP-FLR uses short-term load forecasting with exogenous knowledge, constructs entity-specific load-pattern profiles via clustering, and formulates flexible load regulation as a mixed-integer linear programming problem solved by an MILP solver.
result: Experiments on a regional grid and campus microgrid show regulation deviation reduced by 36.63%-91.87% and participant benefit improved by 44.66% on average.
conclusion: The proposed method effectively improves load regulation accuracy and participant benefits, contributing to smart grid demand response.

title: d'Alembert's Functional Equation And A Globally Convex Free-Action Principle On Positive Paths
authors: Jonathan Washburn Sebastian Pardo-Guerra
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the kinetic action that d'Alembert's functional equation induces on positive paths in [MATH], and prove it strongly convex. Calibrated d'Alembert forces the cosh cost [MATH], i.e.\ [MATH] in the log coordinate [MATH]. Evaluating this log-cost at the log- [MATH] rather than the log-position -- a single postulate (Postulate~) -- yields [MATH], strongly convex under geometric (log-space) interpolation. This convexity has three consequences, none requiring an Euler--Lagrange equation, a Fr\'echet derivative, or a second variation. First, a one-sided chord condition characterizes global minimality. Second, the unique fixed-endpoint minimizer is the uniform-log-velocity path. Third, the action gap obeys an exact Bregman / Pythagorean identity [MATH], sharpened by a quantitative Friedrichs--Poincar\'e bound on [MATH]. It has a dually-flat / Hessian-manifold reading in the additive coordinate [MATH]. \\ This theorem is purely mathematical, and we delimit it. The bridge to Newtonian and rapidity mechanics is , requiring structure beyond Postulate~: a kinematic embedding, a mass coupling, a time calibration, and a Hamiltonian-primary Legendre structure. Granted these, the cosh action recovers the Newtonian small-step limit and the rapidity profile [MATH]; yet the cosh-dual Hamiltonian is the special-relativistic free-particle Hamiltonian (Proposition~), the agreement being one of profile, not an identity of Hamiltonians. Global minimality is a free-sector phenomenon: once a non-affine strictly convex potential is added, joint convexity is lost and the classical stationary-action picture returns.
tldr: This paper proves convexity of a kinetic action derived from d'Alembert's functional equation on positive paths, with applications to mechanics.
motivation: To establish a globally convex free-action principle without Euler-Lagrange equations, and to connect it to Newtonian and relativistic mechanics.
method: The authors study the kinetic action induced by d'Alembert's functional equation, prove strong convexity under geometric interpolation, and derive a Bregman/Pythagorean identity.
result: The action is strongly convex, the unique minimizer is the uniform-log-velocity path, and the action gap satisfies an exact Bregman identity with a Friedrichs-Poincaré bound.
conclusion: The convexity holds only in the free sector; adding a non-affine potential breaks joint convexity, reverting to classical stationary-action principles.

title: The Combined Van-and-Mopeds Routing Problem With Time Windows: Formulation, Variants, And Solution Methods
authors: Pedro Lameiras, Alexandre P. Francisco, Adriano Serrano, C\'atia Vaz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22601v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce and study the Combined Van-and-Mopeds Routing Problem with Time Windows (CVMRPTW), a novel variant of the heterogeneous fleet vehicle routing problem motivated by last-mile parcel delivery in dense European cities. In the CVMRPTW, a single van serves as a mobile base from which on-demand mopeds are deployed to reach customers located in areas inaccessible or inefficient for vans. The primary objective is to minimise the number of mopeds used while guaranteeing that all delivery time windows are met. We propose a Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) formulation that captures vehicle synchronisation, capacity tracking, and time-window compliance through 22 structured constraint families, and extend it to three operationally motivated variants: the standard model, the active-waiting-van variant, and the common-depot variant. A lexicographic two-stage optimisation framework allows secondary objectives-route duration, combined travel time, and combined distance-to be optimised without sacrificing the primary objective. Three graph-sparsification preprocessing techniques reduce the number of variables and constraints by up to 25%. For instances beyond the practical limits of exact solvers, we develop the Cluster-Based Combined Routing (CBCR) heuristic, which decomposes the problem into a clustering phase, a cluster-level exact solve, and a route-reconstruction phase. Computational experiments on real-world instances derived from OpenStreetMap data for Lisbon and Stuttgart show that the MILP solves instances with up to 48 customers to feasibility within one hour, and that the CBCR heuristic extends tractability to instances with up to 80 customers under favourable conditions.
tldr: This paper introduces a new variant of the vehicle routing problem for last-mile delivery using a van and mopeds, with MILP formulation and heuristic solution methods.
motivation: Last-mile parcel delivery in dense European cities faces challenges due to areas inaccessible or inefficient for vans, motivating a combined van-and-moped routing approach.
method: A Mixed-Integer Linear Programming formulation with 22 constraint families is proposed, along with three variants and a Cluster-Based Combined Routing heuristic that decomposes the problem into clustering, exact solve, and route reconstruction.
result: The MILP solves instances up to 48 customers to feasibility within one hour, and the heuristic extends tractability to 80 customers under favorable conditions.
conclusion: The proposed models and heuristic effectively address the combined van-and-moped routing problem, offering practical solutions for last-mile delivery.

title: A Linear Alpha-cut Intervals Based Parsimonious Fuzzy Best-Worst Method With An Application To Warehouse Location Selection
authors: Mohit Kumar Vikas V. Sharma
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22616v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To address computational intensity and crisp weight limitations in the alpha-cut intervals based Fuzzy Best-Worst Method (alpha-FBWM), this research proposes the Linear alpha-cut intervals based Fuzzy Best-Worst Method (Linear alpha-FBWM). By reformulating the non-linear optimization into a single linear programming model, the framework directly determines criteria weights as Triangular Fuzzy Numbers (TFNs) to retain uncertainty. To evaluate weight alignment with decision-makers' initial fuzzy preferences, an Ordinal Preference Violation (OPV) metric is introduced based on the prominence effect. Numerical examples demonstrate that Linear alpha-FBWM minimizes logical violations and matches or outperforms the original alpha-FBWM. To efficiently handle large-scale datasets, we extend this into the Linear alpha-cut intervals based Parsimonious Fuzzy Best-Worst Method (Linear alpha-PFBWM), embedding the linear formulation. This model allows initial alternative ratings as fuzzy numbers and computes non-reference alternative priorities via fuzzy interpolation without early defuzzification. The framework is validated using a literature example and a real-world warehouse selection case study involving 20 alternatives across Gujarat for a multinational paint firm. The integrated approach reduced the required expert evaluations from 185 to 20 initial ratings and 35 pairwise comparisons. This 81.08% reduction in pairwise comparisons proves the framework to be an efficient, reliable, and scalable tool for complex industrial decision-making.
tldr: This paper proposes a linear programming-based fuzzy best-worst method for multi-criteria decision-making, applied to warehouse location selection.
motivation: Existing alpha-cut intervals based Fuzzy Best-Worst Method (alpha-FBWM) is computationally intensive and produces crisp weights, losing uncertainty information.
method: The authors reformulate the non-linear optimization of alpha-FBWM into a single linear programming model to directly obtain triangular fuzzy number weights, and extend it to a parsimonious version that reduces pairwise comparisons.
result: The proposed Linear alpha-PFBWM reduces expert evaluations by 81.08% while maintaining or improving logical consistency compared to alpha-FBWM.
conclusion: The framework is efficient, reliable, and scalable for complex industrial decision-making problems like warehouse location selection.

title: Transform Method For Stochastic Processing And Matching Networks
authors: Sushil Mahavir Varma, Prakirt Jhunjhunwala, Daniela Hurtado-Lange, Siva Theja Maguluri
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22618v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern service systems -- ranging from cloud data centers to ride-hailing platforms -- operate at massive scales where congestion is a critical challenge. Utilizing an operations research approach, these systems are analyzed by modeling them as complex stochastic processes, which are typically understood through process-level convergence to fluid and diffusion limits. However, these methods often prove technically dense and provide limited guidance for finite, practical system scales. The transform method, presented in this tutorial, was recently developed as a unified and tractable framework for the steady-state analysis of Stochastic Processing and Matching Networks (SPNs/SMNs). The transform method overcomes the technical hurdles of process-level convergence by working directly with the pre-limit system. By exploiting the zero-drift property of exponential test functions, the method derives explicit functional equations (acting as a proxy for global balance equations) for the transforms (such as moment-generating functions) of queue-length distributions. This approach provides sharp, non-asymptotic performance guarantees, bridging the gap between theoretical asymptotics and real-world system behavior. Since its introduction in 2020 for load-balancing in data center networks, the transform method has been extended to handle realistic complexities, including customer abandonment, state-dependent arrivals, Markov-modulated arrivals, large-system scale, and multi-dimensional networks with multiple bottlenecks. We survey these theoretical advances and demonstrate their practical relevance across diverse domains, such as matching markets and networked service systems. The transform method provides interpretable bounds tied directly to system parameters, offering a powerful analytical alternative to simulation-heavy or purely asymptotic approaches for system design and control.
tldr: This tutorial presents the transform method for steady-state analysis of stochastic processing and matching networks, focusing on queue-length distributions and performance guarantees.
motivation: Modern service systems like cloud data centers and ride-hailing platforms face congestion challenges that require tractable analytical methods beyond asymptotic limits.
method: The transform method exploits the zero-drift property of exponential test functions to derive functional equations for transforms of queue-length distributions, avoiding process-level convergence.
result: The method provides sharp, non-asymptotic performance guarantees and has been extended to handle customer abandonment, state-dependent arrivals, and multi-dimensional networks.
conclusion: The transform method offers a unified and interpretable analytical alternative to simulation-heavy or purely asymptotic approaches for system design and control.

title: A Resolution Of The Ss--rs--gd Inequalities
authors: Binghui Peng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22620v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Yun, Sra, and Jadbabaie (COLT 2021, open question) conjectured the SS--RS--GD inequalities: for well-conditioned symmetric matrices [MATH], the operators [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH] that encode the expected iterate of single-shuffle SGD, random-reshuffle SGD, and gradient descent on a quadratic finite sum should satisfy \[ \|W_{ss}\|\le \| W_{rs}\|\le \|W_{gd}\|. \] The conjecture is resolved, [MATH] SS-RS inequality fails. Already for [MATH], [MATH], and [MATH], we exhibit explicit PSD matrices whose condition number is arbitrarily close to [MATH], yet [MATH]. [MATH] RS-GD inequality holds. For every symmetric [MATH] with [MATH], one has [MATH]. The proof was found via GPT-5.5 Pro extended prompted by the author.
tldr: This paper resolves a conjecture about operator norms of SGD variants for quadratic finite sums, showing the SS-RS inequality fails while the RS-GD inequality holds.
motivation: The SS-RS-GD inequalities were conjectured to compare the expected iterates of single-shuffle SGD, random-reshuffle SGD, and gradient descent, but their validity was unknown.
method: The author constructs explicit counterexamples for the SS-RS inequality using PSD matrices with high condition numbers, and proves the RS-GD inequality via a spectral analysis.
result: The SS-RS inequality is false in general, while the RS-GD inequality holds for all symmetric matrices with bounded condition number.
conclusion: The conjecture is partially resolved, with implications for understanding the convergence behavior of stochastic optimization methods.

title: Resilience Enhancement Of Electricity-Computing Interdependency System Against Contingency
authors: Zejun Yang Minqiao Zheng
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22623v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electrical power and computing power are highly interdependent especially due to the AI revolution. This dependency is largely underestimated during normal and recovery operation. To address this issue, an Electricity-Computing Interdependency System (ECIS) is developed in this paper, which first quantifies the interdependencies between ECIS and other critical infrastructures. The data center (DC) is modeled as a facility that transforms electrical power into computing power, and a recovery optimization strategy for ECIS is then proposed considering electrical power constraints, computing power supply, and infrastructure interdependencies. The case study demonstrates that the proposed strategy dynamically adjusts the DC electrical power quota according to system states, improving system resilience by more than 20% during power shortage.
tldr: This paper proposes a recovery optimization strategy for an electricity-computing interdependency system to enhance resilience during power shortages.
motivation: The interdependency between electrical power and computing power is often underestimated, especially during recovery operations, leading to reduced system resilience.
method: The authors model a data center as a facility that transforms electrical power into computing power and develop a recovery optimization strategy that dynamically adjusts data center electrical power quotas considering power constraints and infrastructure interdependencies.
result: The proposed strategy improves system resilience by more than 20% during power shortages, as demonstrated in a case study.
conclusion: The dynamic adjustment of data center power quotas based on system states can significantly enhance the resilience of electricity-computing interdependency systems.

title: Spectral Analysis Of Heavy-Ball Q-value Iteration
authors: Donghwan Lee
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22627v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the convergence and acceleration of Q-value iteration (QVI) with momentum, or heavy-ball QVI. Although acceleration of value iteration has been studied extensively, there has been less work on the acceleration of heavy-ball QVI for control tasks. We analyze heavy-ball QVI from the viewpoint of switched linear system (SLS) theory and the joint spectral radius (JSR). First, we convert heavy-ball QVI into an exact SLS and interpret its convergence through the JSR. We also study, in JSR-based terms, conditions under which heavy-ball QVI can be faster than standard QVI.
tldr: This paper analyzes the convergence of heavy-ball Q-value iteration using switched linear system theory and joint spectral radius.
motivation: Acceleration of value iteration for control tasks is important, but heavy-ball QVI has not been thoroughly analyzed.
method: The paper converts heavy-ball QVI into an exact switched linear system and studies its convergence via joint spectral radius.
result: Conditions under which heavy-ball QVI can be faster than standard QVI are derived in JSR-based terms.
conclusion: The analysis provides a new perspective on accelerating Q-value iteration with momentum.

title: Network Analysis Reveals Phase Transitions In Agro-food Nitrogen Systems With Contrasting Feeding Capacity And Land Requirement
authors: Adrien Fauste-Gay, Jeremie Unterberger, Olivier Vidal, Lauriane Mouysset
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agro-food transitions are commonly assessed using optimization models or scenario approaches that return a single feasible configuration. These approaches provide estimates of system performance but limited information on feasible nitrogen cycling configurations. In this study, we develop a network-based modelling framework to characterize alternative steady-state configurations of agro-food nitrogen systems and identify phase transitions between these configurations. We formulate a continuous-time compartmental network model in which production, allocation, recycling, and losses are represented as mass-conserving flows. The system is analyzed under steady-state conditions. A coarse-graining procedure identifies dominant recycling cycles and derives aggregate indicators describing system configuration. The model is parameterized using French reference data and applied to case studies covering fertilization, livestock, and dietary patterns. The analysis identifies distinct steady-state configurations of the nitrogen network, separated by phase transitions in dominant recycling structures. These transitions correspond to changes in system performance indicators. For the French reference system, cropland-based feeding capacity is about 8.7 people per hectare of cropland (depending on constraints), while strict dietary autonomy requires about 19.7 million hectares of agricultural land. Reducing synthetic fertilization without changes in diet or nitrogen sourcing leads to higher land requirements or greater dependence on external inputs. The framework provides a method for mapping feasible nitrogen system configurations and analyzing phase transitions in agro-food nitrogen networks under alternative parameters and constraints.
tldr: This paper develops a network model to analyze nitrogen cycling in agro-food systems, identifying phase transitions between steady-state configurations.
motivation: To characterize alternative feasible configurations of agro-food nitrogen systems and understand transitions between them, beyond single-optimization approaches.
