method: A continuous-time compartmental network model with mass-conserving flows is formulated, analyzed under steady-state, and coarse-grained to identify dominant recycling cycles.
result: Distinct steady-state configurations separated by phase transitions are found; for France, cropland feeding capacity is ~8.7 people/ha and dietary autonomy requires ~19.7 million ha.
conclusion: The framework maps feasible nitrogen system configurations and phase transitions, showing trade-offs between fertilization, diet, and land requirements.

title: Mean-field Model For Pollution Abatement Via Cap And Trade Mechanism
authors: Giacomo Lanaro Ofelia Bonesini
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a mean-field model of competitive firms operating under an AK production technology, where output is proportional to capital and production generates emissions. In this setting, we introduce a regulator whose objective is the reduction of cumulative emissions, in the spirit of Emission Trading Systems (ETS), where firms must hold and trade permits to cover their emissions in a regulated market. The regulator acts as a central planner and controls the supply of permits, balancing emission reduction and aggregate output. Permits are allocated through a dynamic auction mechanism that adjusts supply in real time to achieve both market efficiency and the regulator's long-term goals. The regulator and the firms interact through the endogenous permit price, which is determined by the regulator's policy and affects firms' optimal strategies via the market clearing condition. The regulator's optimal policy is derived within a Mean-Field Control (MFC) framework. Exploiting the linear-quadratic structure and the presence of common noise, we characterise the equilibrium via a system of coupled FBSDEs and associated Riccati equations. Our results provide a tractable characterisation of optimal permit allocation policies in large economies and offer insights into the design of efficient emission trading mechanisms.
tldr: This paper models pollution abatement via cap-and-trade using mean-field control, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The authors aim to design optimal permit allocation policies in large economies to reduce cumulative emissions while maintaining aggregate output.
method: They formulate a mean-field control problem with linear-quadratic structure and common noise, solving coupled FBSDEs and Riccati equations.
result: A tractable characterization of optimal permit allocation policies is derived, providing insights into efficient emission trading mechanisms.
conclusion: The framework offers a rigorous approach to cap-and-trade regulation, but is unrelated to quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Upper And Lower Approximations Of The Second Order. Exhausters Of The Second Order
authors: I. M. Prudnikov
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The upper and lower approximations of the second order are defined for a function differentiable in the directions. Exhausters of the second order are introduced. The relation between the second-order Frechet subdifferentials and the second-order exhausters is given. A rule for constructing exhausters of the first and second orders is given for Lipschitz functions.Necessary and sufficient extremum conditions through exhausters are given. It is discussed about the use of Exhausters in optimization.
tldr: This paper introduces second-order upper and lower approximations and exhausters for directionally differentiable functions, with applications to optimization.
motivation: To extend the concept of exhausters to second order for analyzing nonsmooth functions and deriving optimality conditions.
method: Defines second-order approximations and exhausters, relates them to second-order Frechet subdifferentials, and provides construction rules for Lipschitz functions.
result: Necessary and sufficient extremum conditions are given using second-order exhausters.
conclusion: Second-order exhausters provide a tool for optimization of nonsmooth functions.

title: Variational Formulations For Fractional Integral And Differential Equations
authors: Delfim F. M. Torres
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given a fractional-order linear equation [MATH], we define an appropriate symmetric bilinear form so that the fractional operator [MATH] is symmetric with respect to that bilinear form. Using the bilinear form, we then define a functional of the fractional calculus of variations proving that the solutions of the given fractional-order equation are critical points of the fractional variational functional. In the case of fractional integral equations, the provided bilinear form is non-degenerate, and all critical points are solutions of the given equation. In the case of fractional differential equations, a relation with the least-squares method is obtained.
tldr: This paper develops variational formulations for fractional integral and differential equations by constructing symmetric bilinear forms.
motivation: To provide a variational framework for fractional-order equations, enabling the use of calculus of variations techniques.
method: Defines an appropriate symmetric bilinear form such that the fractional operator is symmetric, then constructs a functional whose critical points correspond to solutions.
result: For fractional integral equations, the bilinear form is non-degenerate and all critical points are solutions; for differential equations, a relation with least-squares is obtained.
conclusion: The variational approach successfully characterizes solutions of fractional equations as critical points, offering a new perspective on fractional problems.

title: On The Algebraic Complexity Of Optimal Polynomial Approximation Constants
authors: Filip Filipovi\'c, R\'emi G\'eraud-Stewart, David Naccacheand Aleksa Veli\v{c}kovi\'c
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the algebraic nature of constants arising from Chebyshev equiripple (minimax) polynomial approximation of [MATH] norms on [MATH]. For the Euclidean case [MATH], we compute equiripple solutions from degree~1 through~8 and determine exact minimal polynomials and Galois groups for degrees~1 and~2 in both absolute and relative error formulations. We find a sharp phase transition: the degree-1 constants are solvable by radicals (Galois groups [MATH], [MATH]), while the degree-2 constants provably are not (Galois groups [MATH], [MATH]). We explain this transition by a structural dichotomy between decoupling and coupling of critical points, and extend the analysis to [MATH] norms, where the minimal polynomial degree jumps to~246. A general impossibility result follows from Hilbert's irreducibility theorem. We also develop a theory of piecewise equiripple approximation with jointly optimized breakpoints, proving that each doubling of the number of subintervals gains [MATH] bits of accuracy at no additional arithmetic cost. These results establish a previously unobserved connection between Chebyshev approximation theory and the non-solvability of algebraic equations.
tldr: This paper studies the algebraic complexity of optimal polynomial approximation constants, connecting Chebyshev approximation theory to Galois theory.
motivation: To understand the algebraic nature of constants arising from minimax polynomial approximation and to determine whether they are solvable by radicals.
method: Computes equiripple solutions for degrees 1 through 8, determines minimal polynomials and Galois groups, and extends analysis to L^p norms using Hilbert's irreducibility theorem.
result: Degree-1 constants are solvable by radicals, while degree-2 constants are not; a phase transition is explained by decoupling vs coupling of critical points.
conclusion: The work establishes a new connection between Chebyshev approximation theory and the non-solvability of algebraic equations, with implications for numerical analysis.

title: The Capacitated $p$-Location Problem With Territorial Coverage Constraint: Efficient Solution And Case Study
authors: Felipe Albuquerque, Rosa Figueiredo, Cyrille Genre-Grandpierre
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22666v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies the Capacitated [MATH]-Location Problem (C[MATH]LP) and its extensions incorporating equity considerations. In location science, the [MATH]-Median problem ([MATH]MP) is a classical model which selects [MATH] facilities from a finite set of candidates to serve a set of customers minimizing total allocation costs. The C[MATH]LP which includes the Capacitated p-Median Problem (C[MATH]MP) and its relaxed variant (C[MATH]MP[MATH]), extends the [MATH]MP by incorporating capacity constraints on facilities.We first introduce the C[MATH]LP with Territorial Coverage Constraints (C[MATH]LP-TC), a extension of the CpLP that enforces equity considering the spatial units. Building on this, we propose the multi-scale variant (C[MATH]LP-MTC), which generalizes territorial coverage constraints across nested spatial scales, allowing equity to be enforced simultaneously at multiple levels of spatial aggregation. A strengthened Integer Linear Programming (ILP) formulation with valid inequalities is presented. In addition, we develop the Random Sampling Spatial Voting (RSSV) matheuristic, which integrates a heuristic reduction phase with the strengthened ILP. The method is flexible, requires minimal parameter tuning, and remains accessible to non specialist users. Computational experiments on benchmark and real world instances demonstrate its efficiency and reliability. The results also demonstrate the impact of equity territorial based constraints on fairness in location planning.
tldr: This paper studies a capacitated p-location problem with territorial coverage constraints, proposing an ILP formulation and a matheuristic for equitable facility location.
motivation: Classical location models often ignore equity, leading to unfair service distribution. The authors aim to incorporate territorial coverage constraints to enforce fairness across spatial units.
method: They introduce the Capacitated p-Location Problem with Territorial Coverage Constraints (CpLP-TC) and a multi-scale variant, develop a strengthened ILP with valid inequalities, and propose the Random Sampling Spatial Voting (RSSV) matheuristic combining heuristic reduction with ILP.
result: Computational experiments on benchmark and real-world instances show the method is efficient and reliable, and demonstrate the impact of equity constraints on fairness in location planning.
conclusion: The proposed approach effectively integrates equity into location planning, offering a flexible tool for practitioners.

title: Classification Of Derived Azumaya Algebras Over Derived Smooth Manifolds Via Derived Brauer Groups
authors: Christopher Tropp Yimu Mao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22668v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a derived smooth manifold [MATH] in the sense of Spivak, we pull back To\"en's categorical derived Brauer stack along the forgetful functor from simplicial [MATH]-rings to connective simplicial commutative rings and then stackify on the open site of [MATH]. The resulting categorical Brauer stack has the homotopy type \[ _X \simeq K(,1) \times B^2GL_1(_X). \] Consequently its group of stackified Brauer classes is \[ dBr(X):=\pi_0\Gamma(X,_X) \cong H^1(X,) \times \pi_0\Gamma(X,B^2GL_1(_X)), \] where [MATH] is the sheaf of derived units. The usual formula with [MATH] is recovered when the structure sheaf is discrete. This shows that the pullback categorical Brauer invariant is governed by the full homotopy type of the derived unit sheaf.
tldr: This paper studies derived Azumaya algebras over derived smooth manifolds and computes the derived Brauer group.
motivation: To understand the classification of derived Azumaya algebras via derived Brauer groups in the context of derived differential geometry.
method: Pulls back Toën's categorical derived Brauer stack along a forgetful functor and stackifies on the open site of a derived smooth manifold.
result: The categorical Brauer stack has homotopy type K(ℤ,1) × B²GL₁(𝒪_X), and the group of stackified Brauer classes is H¹(X, ℤ) × π₀Γ(X, B²GL₁(𝒪_X)).
conclusion: The derived Brauer invariant is governed by the full homotopy type of the derived unit sheaf, recovering the usual formula when the structure sheaf is discrete.

title: The Bi-UF Positive Conjecture For Quadratic Monogenic Semirings And Related Progress
authors: Felix Gotti, Omar Graia, Darren Han, Hengrui Liang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A complex semiring is a subset of the complex plane that is closed under the standard addition and multiplication of complex numbers and contains both [MATH] and [MATH]. A complex semiring [MATH] is called a bi-UFS if both its additive monoid [MATH] and its multiplicative monoid [MATH] are unique factorization monoids (UFM). The Bi-UF Positive Conjecture states that [MATH] is the only subsemiring of the nonnegative cone of the real line that is a bi-UFS. In this paper, we prove that no simple semiring extension of [MATH] by a quadratic algebraic number is a bi-UFS, identifying a natural class of complex semirings satisfying the statement of the Bi-UF Positive Conjecture. We also identify another class of complex semirings satisfying the statement of the Bi-UF Positive Conjecture. Then we extend the statement of the Bi-UF Positive Conjecture by motivated by a structural theorem we established for semidomains whose additive monoid are finite-rank free commutative monoids. Finally, we consider the bi-HF property, which is a relaxed version of the bi-UF property. We prove that [MATH] is the only positive rational semidomain having the bi-HF property, and we provide two methods to construct bi-HFS complex semirings that are distinct from [MATH].
tldr: This paper studies unique factorization properties of complex semirings, specifically quadratic monogenic semirings, which is unrelated to quantum information theory.
motivation: The Bi-UF Positive Conjecture concerns algebraic structures in complex semirings, with no connection to quantum information, thermodynamics, networks, or hybrid quantum systems.
method: The authors prove that no simple semiring extension of the nonnegative reals by a quadratic algebraic number is a bi-UFS, and identify classes of semirings satisfying the conjecture.
result: They show that the only positive rational semidomain with the bi-HF property is the nonnegative rationals, and provide methods to construct bi-HFS complex semirings.
conclusion: The work contributes to pure mathematics (semiring theory) and does not intersect with the user's research interests.

title: Kernel-Type Fractional Extensions Of Reverse Callebaut, Rogers H\"older And Cauchy Schwarz Inequalities On Time Scales
authors: Gobinda Ghosh Nimai Sarkar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22670v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we establish kernel-type fractional extensions of reverse Callebaut, Rogers--H\"older and Cauchy--Schwarz inequalities on time scales. The proposed results are formulated by means of a nonnegative kernel operator associated with the diamond-[MATH] integral, which enables the inclusion of memory effects within the framework of dynamic inequalities. By choosing particular kernels and time scales, the obtained inequalities reduce to their continuous, discrete and quantum counterparts. Moreover, when the kernel is taken as the identity kernel, the results recover the corresponding classical diamond-[MATH] dynamic inequalities. Several consequences are derived as special cases, including fractional reverse Cauchy--Schwarz inequalities and weighted reverse Rogers--H\"older inequalities. The results provide a unified approach for studying reverse inequalities in continuous, discrete, quantum and fractional dynamic settings and may be applied to obtain a priori estimates for Volterra-type and delay dynamic equations.
tldr: This paper establishes kernel-type fractional extensions of reverse Callebaut, Rogers-Hölder, and Cauchy-Schwarz inequalities on time scales.
motivation: To unify and generalize reverse inequalities in continuous, discrete, quantum, and fractional dynamic settings, incorporating memory effects via a nonnegative kernel operator.
method: The authors use a nonnegative kernel operator associated with the diamond-α integral on time scales to formulate fractional extensions of classical inequalities.
result: The proposed inequalities reduce to continuous, discrete, and quantum counterparts for specific kernels and time scales, and recover classical diamond-α dynamic inequalities when the kernel is identity.
conclusion: The results provide a unified approach for studying reverse inequalities in various dynamic settings and may be applied to obtain a priori estimates for Volterra-type and delay dynamic equations.

title: Coupling Of Local And Nonlocal Problems Using Local Boundary Conditions
authors: Burak Aksoylu, Fatih Celiker, Patrick Diehl
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22672v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a novel coupling method for local and nonlocal diffusion problems in 1D. Unlike other methods, our coupling method exclusively uses local boundary conditions. This is possible because our nonlocal operators enforce them by construction. Leveraging this advantageous property, we construct a seamless coupling that is remarkably natural. The utilization of local boundary conditions allows for the transfer of well-established numerical methods from local problems to nonlocal ones. Our local-to-nonlocal coupling method is inspired by the domain decomposition method, which we would like to transfer to nonlocal problems. The main result of our study is the construction of a local-to-nonlocal coupling method with a quantifiable [MATH] convergence that holds for an arbitrary solution. For discretization of the local and nonlocal problems, the finite element method and the Galerkin projection are employed, respectively. We verify our convergence rate with extensive numerical experiments.
tldr: This paper presents a coupling method for local and nonlocal diffusion problems using only local boundary conditions.
motivation: To develop a seamless coupling between local and nonlocal diffusion models that leverages local boundary conditions, enabling the transfer of numerical methods from local to nonlocal problems.
method: The coupling method is inspired by domain decomposition; local problems are discretized with finite elements and nonlocal problems with Galerkin projection.
result: The method achieves quantifiable convergence that holds for arbitrary solutions, verified by numerical experiments.
conclusion: The proposed coupling method is natural and effective, allowing well-established numerical techniques to be applied to nonlocal problems.

title: Convexifying Mean-Field Control: An Occupation-Measure And Frank-Wolfe Approach
authors: Di Yu, Sixiong You, Chaoying Pei
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22678v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large-scale robotic swarms motivate the use of mean-field control (MFC). Classical partial differential equation (PDE)-based formulations provide a principled framework but can become computationally challenging in higher dimensions, whereas machine learning achieves scalability at the cost of approximation and guarantees. In this work, we establish an optimization-based framework that lifts the MFC problem into the space of occupation measures, resulting in a convex relaxation formulated as an optimization over measures. The resulting problem is solved using a Frank-Wolfe (FW) algorithm in the measure space, with each iteration reduced to a tractable optimal control problem. This approach retains the O(1/k) convergence rate of FW, avoids discretization of the state space, and naturally incorporates interaction and safety constraints. Numerical experiments demonstrate agreement with analytic and PDE-based baselines in two dimensions and show that the method scales to three-dimensional environments with multiple obstacles, where standard grid-based PDE solvers become impractical. A full 3D instance with ten obstacles is solved in minutes on a standard workstation, underscoring the practicality and scalability of the proposed framework.
tldr: This paper proposes a convex optimization framework for mean-field control using occupation measures and a Frank-Wolfe algorithm, targeting large-scale robotic swarms.
motivation: Classical PDE-based mean-field control methods become computationally challenging in higher dimensions, while machine learning approaches sacrifice guarantees. The authors aim for a scalable, principled optimization approach.
method: The MFC problem is lifted into the space of occupation measures, yielding a convex relaxation solved via a Frank-Wolfe algorithm in measure space, with each iteration reduced to a tractable optimal control problem.
result: The method retains O(1/k) convergence, avoids state-space discretization, and scales to 3D environments with multiple obstacles, solving instances in minutes on a standard workstation.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a practical and scalable alternative to PDE-based MFC for high-dimensional robotic swarm control.

title: Can The Perfect Swiss Alphorn Be Designed? A Combination Of Reduced Basis Method And Machine Learning For Shape Optimization
authors: Fabio Marcinn\`o, Cl\'ement Froidevaux, Leonardo Bocchieri, Riccardo Tenderini, Gerald Pot, Simone Deparis
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the shape optimization of a Swiss alphorn to achieve resonance frequencies as close as possible to prescribed target notes. We construct an accurate geometric model of the alphorn based on both experimental measurements and imaging techniques. The latter are used to reconstruct geometric information where direct measures are not available. The resulting 3D model is meshed using a fully structured approach. Then, we introduce a geometry-parametrized finite element (FE) formulation of the Helmholtz equation enabling the application of the Reduced Basis Method (RBM) to efficiently generate a large dataset of simulations, in which each set of geometric parameters corresponds to a specific set of resonance frequencies (notes). This dataset enables the training of machine learning (ML) models for forward prediction of resonance frequencies from geometric parameters, as well as inverse design, where geometries are estimated to achieve specified target notes.
tldr: This paper uses reduced basis methods and machine learning to optimize the shape of a Swiss alphorn for desired resonance frequencies.
motivation: To achieve perfect musical notes in alphorn design by combining computational methods.
method: Constructs a 3D geometric model from measurements, uses parametrized finite element simulations with reduced basis method to generate data, then trains ML models for forward and inverse prediction.
result: Demonstrates efficient generation of simulation data and accurate prediction of resonance frequencies from geometric parameters.
conclusion: The approach successfully enables shape optimization for acoustic instruments, but has no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Proximal Relations And Maximal Equicontinuous Factors For Non-autonomous Dynamical Systems
authors: Saksham Malik, Mohammad Salman, Ruchi Das
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22849v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies proximal-type relations and maximal equicontinuous factors for non-autonomous dynamical systems on compact metric spaces. Two classes of systems are considered: systems generated by uniformly convergent sequences of maps and periodic systems. For uniformly convergent generators, collective convergence and uniform rigidity imply that the regional proximal relation for the non-autonomous system is equal to the regional proximal relation for the limit autonomous system and if the limit system is equicontinuous, then the proximality relation for the non-autonomous system is equal to the proximal relation for the autonomous limit system. In the same setting, the kernel of the maximal equicontinuous factor is identified as the smallest closed equivalence relation containing the autonomous equicontinuous structure relation of the corresponding autonomous system and preserved by all generators. For periodic systems, regional proximality and Banach proximality are determined by the period map, yielding a criterion in terms of mean equicontinuity and the relation of sensitivity in the mean. Examples show that the hypotheses used in these results are necessary.
tldr: This paper studies proximal relations and maximal equicontinuous factors for non-autonomous dynamical systems on compact metric spaces.
motivation: To understand the structure of non-autonomous dynamical systems, particularly how proximality and equicontinuity relate to the limit or periodic behavior of the generating maps.
method: The authors analyze two classes of systems: those generated by uniformly convergent sequences of maps and periodic systems. They use topological dynamics concepts such as regional proximal relations, Banach proximality, and mean equicontinuity.
result: For uniformly convergent generators, the regional proximal relation equals that of the limit autonomous system under collective convergence and uniform rigidity; for periodic systems, proximality is determined by the period map and related to mean equicontinuity.
conclusion: The results provide criteria for equicontinuity and sensitivity in non-autonomous systems, with examples showing necessity of hypotheses.

title: H$_1$-iss Analysis And Boundary Control Design For Coupled Linear ODEs And Hyperbolic PDEs
authors: Franthiescolly Vieira de Carvalho, Daniel Coutinho, Gustavo de Andrade, Christophe Prieur, Mohamed Maghenem
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22881v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers the general problem of the design of boundary controllers for distributed parameter systems. The control objectives are the asymptotic stability of the closed-loop system, as well as the disturbance attenuation of exogenous disturbances affecting the measurements and boundary conditions. More specifically, this work studies input-to-state stability (ISS) and stabilization for systems governed by coupled linear ordinary differential equations (ODEs) and homogeneous linear hyperbolic partial differential equations (PDEs), where actuation, sensing, and disturbance inputs are located at the system boundaries. First, we extend a previously established Lyapunov-based ISS condition for a similar class of systems to the H[MATH] setting under mild assumptions on the disturbance inputs. This extension not only ensures that the H[MATH]-norm of the system states driven by non-vanishing disturbances and compatible initial conditions are bounded, but also provides an upper bound on the system H[MATH]-norm. Subsequently, these theoretical results are applied to derive stability analysis and control design conditions expressed in terms of linear matrix inequalities. Numerical examples are provided to illustrate the effectiveness and potential of the proposed approach.
tldr: This paper designs boundary controllers for coupled ODEs and hyperbolic PDEs, focusing on ISS and H-infinity stability.
motivation: To extend Lyapunov-based ISS conditions to H-infinity setting for coupled linear ODEs and hyperbolic PDEs with boundary disturbances.
method: Extends a Lyapunov-based ISS condition to H-infinity setting and derives LMI-based stability analysis and control design conditions.
result: Provides H-infinity norm bounds for system states and LMI conditions for controller design, validated by numerical examples.
conclusion: The proposed approach effectively ensures asymptotic stability and disturbance attenuation for the considered class of distributed parameter systems.

title: ReCon: A Resource-Constrained Benchmark For LLM-Based Cybersecurity Compliance Across Ingestion And Retrieval Pipelines
authors: Rohit Negi, Rishik Jain, Soumyo V Chakarborty, Amit Negi, Sandeep K Shukla
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22885v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: With the increasingly aggressive cyber threat landscape for governments, businesses, and institutions, as information and/or cybersecurity implementations are increasingly under scrutiny by regulators, it has been pointed out that governance failure is one of the major reasons for a weakened cybersecurity posture. A major component of Cyber/information security governance is the development, adoption, and implementation of a comprehensive information and/or cyber security policy document. The policy document must be in compliance with international or national standards and, if possible, with regulatory guidelines. However, it is often observed that policy documents are often incomplete with respect to industry standards or regulations and require revision when subjected to a thorough audit. Identifying the gaps between the controls and processes documented in the policy and those required in the regulations or standards necessitates extensive manual effort. The advent of Generative AI tools such as Large Language Models (LLMs) led to use of LLMs and Agentic AI tools to automate such compliance checks, as seen in a few research publications in recent times. However, such reported use of LLMs are experimented with high resource environments such as expensive GPUs and memory based servers. For smaller organizations such expensive compute platform may not be easily available. In this article, we benchmark the compliance checking tasks on LLMs that do not require GPU and high memory usage and the effectiveness of such resource constrained LLMs in compliance checking. Our experiments demonstrated that the low resource LLMs can provide good agreement/accuracy in compliance checking of policy documents against standards by experimenting with ISO 27002:2022 controls against multiple policy documents.
tldr: This paper benchmarks resource-constrained LLMs for cybersecurity compliance checking against ISO 27002:2022.
motivation: Small organizations lack expensive GPUs for LLM-based compliance automation, so evaluating low-resource LLMs is necessary.
method: The authors test multiple low-resource LLMs on compliance checking of policy documents against ISO 27002:2022 controls.
result: Low-resource LLMs achieve good accuracy in compliance checking.
conclusion: Resource-constrained LLMs can effectively automate cybersecurity compliance checks for smaller organizations.

title: A Modular Cyber Range Platform For Smart Energy Systems
authors: Vasilis Ieropoulos, Theofanis Eleftheriadis, Kyriakos Christou, Philippos Isaia, Maria Michalopoulou, Angelos K. Marnerides, Christos Laoudias, Maria K. Michael
abstract: ArXiv:2607.22943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern critical infrastructure requires realistic training tools that bridge the gap between digital vulnerabilities and physical consequences. This paper introduces a lightweight, modular Cyber Range (CR) designed to simulate Information Technology (IT) and Operational Technology (OT) environments with high fidelity. Using the FastAPI framework as backend and Quick Emulator (QEMU)/Kernel-based Virtual Machine (KVM) virtualisation, the platform employs a YAML-based engine to automatically deploy complex networks on standard hardware with minimal overhead. To demonstrate its capabilities, we present a Photovoltaic (PV) Plant scenario set in a fictional smart city. The scenario follows a multi-stage attack that begins with the compromise of a home Internet of Things (IoT) device and escalates into a major power outage at a military base. The proposed CR, natively supports industrial protocols such as Modbus/TCP and Message Queuing Telemetry Transport (MQTT) and includes a "Green Team" framework for evaluating human performance during crisis situations. This paper describes the system architecture, automated setup, protocol-simulation capabilities, and scenario design.
tldr: This paper presents a modular cyber range platform for simulating cyber-physical attacks on smart energy systems, focusing on IT/OT security training.
motivation: Modern critical infrastructure requires realistic training tools that bridge digital vulnerabilities and physical consequences.
method: The platform uses FastAPI, QEMU/KVM virtualization, and a YAML-based engine to deploy complex networks; it supports industrial protocols like Modbus/TCP and MQTT and includes a Green Team framework for human performance evaluation.
result: A photovoltaic plant scenario demonstrates a multi-stage attack from IoT compromise to power outage, validating the platform's capabilities.
conclusion: The proposed cyber range provides a lightweight, modular solution for cybersecurity training in smart energy systems.

title: Mask2Shield: Strengthening Llm Safety Against Neuron-Pruning Attacks
authors: Ying Jincheng, Minghui Xu, Yinhao Xiao, Xiuzhen Cheng, Wencheng Yang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23015v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are safety-aligned before deployment to reduce harmful content generation. Yet neuron-level pruning attacks show that refusal can depend on a small set of removable units: disabling them can remove safety behavior while leaving much of the model usable. To address this problem, we introduce Mask2Shield (M2S), a masked-forward alignment method that trains a model under this functional pruning. The masked student must recover a safe refusal through the remaining computation, while a frozen, unmasked teacher supplies complete benign answers to limit capability drift. Across ten model configurations, M2S reduces successful recomputed pruning attacks from 80--279 to 1--44 out of 313 prompts while generally preserving four capability benchmarks. We also evaluate M2S with TwinBreak, which uses a different neuron-selection rule and iterative pruning procedure. Together, these results show that M2S makes targeted pruning less effective by reducing reliance on a small, removable safety-neuron set.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to make large language models robust against neuron-pruning attacks that remove safety alignment.
motivation: Neuron-level pruning attacks can disable safety behavior in LLMs by removing a small set of units, posing a security risk.
method: Mask2Shield uses masked-forward alignment where a student model is trained to recover safe refusal under functional pruning, guided by a frozen teacher model.
result: The method reduces successful attacks from 80-279 to 1-44 out of 313 prompts across ten model configurations while preserving capability benchmarks.
conclusion: Mask2Shield effectively reduces reliance on a small set of safety neurons, making targeted pruning less effective.

title: Electromagnetic Neural Network For Direction-of-Arrival Estimation
authors: Shining Lin, Jiancheng An, Lu Gan, Victor C. M. Leung, Mehdi Bennis, M\'erouane Debbah, Tie Jun Cui
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate and real-time direction of arrival (DOA) estimation is crucial for beamforming in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communication systems. However, the existing high-precision DOA estimation algorithms encounter high computational complexity when implemented on a UAV with on-board signal processing constraints. To tackle this issue, an electromagnetic neural network (EMNN) is developed for DOA estimation, which is capable of generating the angular spectrum of the incident signal based solely on amplitude observation. Specifically, the proposed EMNN consists of two components: a stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIM) is mounted on the UAV, and each meta-atom is an artificial neuron that can process signals in the electromagnetic domain with low energy consumption and ultra-fast computing speed. Furthermore, a fully connected layer is cascaded to process the received amplitude signal, enhancing the non-linear extraction and representational ability of EMNN. Moreover, to reduce the computational complexity and observation snapshots required for high-resolution DOA estimation, we develop a hierarchical DOA estimation framework, which involves two stages for conducting coarse and fine DOA estimation, respectively. For each stage, EMNN is trained on randomly generated training samples and their corresponding spectra to achieve the desired estimation goal. Finally, the simulation results validate that the proposed EMNN achieves approximately 13 dB gain in classification error reduction over the conventional beamforming (CBF) method in dual-signal scenarios, albeit its lower cost and radio frequency (RF)-related power consumption.
tldr: This paper proposes an electromagnetic neural network for direction-of-arrival estimation in UAV communication systems.
motivation: High-precision DOA estimation algorithms have high computational complexity, which is challenging for UAVs with limited onboard processing capabilities.
method: The EMNN uses a stacked intelligent metasurface as artificial neurons for electromagnetic-domain signal processing, followed by a fully connected layer for nonlinear extraction, and a hierarchical two-stage coarse-to-fine estimation framework.
result: Simulations show the EMNN achieves about 13 dB gain in classification error reduction over conventional beamforming in dual-signal scenarios, with lower cost and power consumption.
conclusion: The EMNN offers an efficient and low-power solution for real-time DOA estimation on UAVs.

title: On The Power Of Deception In Repeated Games
authors: Saba Ahmadi, Avrim Blum, Dimitar Chakarov, Melissa Dutz
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23049v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In repeated games, opponents often predict what we'll do next by looking at what we have done so far. This allows us to deceive them: we can deliberately behave one way for a period of time to shape their expectations, then switch strategies to profit from the induced response. We study deception in repeated two-player normal-form games against count-based learners, whose behavior depends only on how often we have played each action in the past. We formalize deceptive and non-deceptive play, and introduce the notion of a deception bonus, the payoff gain of the best deceptive strategy over the best fixed mixed strategy. We establish structural results on deception in general-sum games. We design exact dynamic programs for optimizing against any count-based learner when the action space or opponent's memory is small, and develop approximation algorithms for settings where the opponent's memory or the time horizon is large. We also provide an approximation algorithm for learning to deceive an opponent whose count-based learning rule is unknown. To complement our algorithmic results, we show that approximating the optimal deceptive payoff against the classic Empirical Risk Minimization (ERM) learning rule is NP-hard, including obtaining any constant-factor approximation or even a [MATH]-additive approximation for any [MATH]. Finally, we empirically measure the deception bonus in random games with i.i.d. payoffs.
tldr: This paper studies deception in repeated games against count-based learners, with algorithmic and complexity results.
motivation: Understanding how to deceive opponents in repeated games can inform strategic decision-making in adversarial settings.
method: The authors formalize deceptive play, define a deception bonus, and design dynamic programming and approximation algorithms for optimizing against count-based learners, while also proving NP-hardness for the ERM rule.
result: They provide structural results, exact and approximation algorithms, and hardness results for computing optimal deceptive strategies.
conclusion: Deception can provide a significant payoff advantage, but computing optimal strategies is computationally hard in some cases.

title: Glst: Defending Confidence-Driven V2x Collaborative Perception Against Stealthy Multi-Attacker Feature Injection
authors: Ji He, Ying Wang, Lijie Zheng, Xinghui Zhu, Yulong Shen, Xiaohong Jiang
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Collaborative perception (CP) improves autonomous-driving perception by enabling connected vehicles to exchange intermediate features via V2X. Confidence-driven sparse communication reduces bandwidth by transmitting only perception-critical spatial regions, but creates a security risk: once a collaborator is compromised, malicious features in high-confidence or ego-uncertain regions may be preferentially selected and amplified during fusion. Using Where2comm as a representative framework, we show that the proposed Pretend Benign attack exploits its spatial-confidence mechanism by injecting stealthy perturbations into uncertain yet perception-critical regions, substantially degrading 3D object detection while preserving benign-like feature characteristics. Beyond this attack-framework pair, we identify a broader weakness of existing trust-based defenses: their reliance primarily on a single consistency signal leaves them vulnerable when multiple attackers form a pseudo-consensus that biases trust estimation. We therefore propose Global-Local Structural Trust (GLST), a lightweight defense that assesses collaborator reliability through three complementary perspectives: global feature consistency, multi-scale local residual consistency, and structural consistency with ego-side semantic topology. The resulting trust scores guide feature fusion to suppress unreliable collaborators. Experiments on OPV2V show that GLST achieves competitive performance against single-attacker Pretend Benign attacks and substantially stronger robustness in multi-attacker settings. Under a four-attacker Pretend Benign attack, GLST maintains 0.69 AP@0.3, whereas existing single-signal defenses degrade severely. GLST also remains effective against gradient-based attacks such as PGD, indicating that multi-level trust modeling is essential for securing confidence-driven CP.
tldr: This paper proposes a defense against stealthy feature injection attacks in V2X collaborative perception for autonomous driving.
motivation: Confidence-driven sparse communication in collaborative perception is vulnerable to attacks where compromised collaborators inject malicious features that are preferentially selected and amplified.
method: The authors propose Global-Local Structural Trust (GLST), a lightweight defense that assesses collaborator reliability through global feature consistency, multi-scale local residual consistency, and structural consistency with ego-side semantic topology.
result: GLST maintains 0.69 AP@0.3 under a four-attacker Pretend Benign attack, outperforming existing single-signal defenses that degrade severely.
conclusion: Multi-level trust modeling is essential for securing confidence-driven collaborative perception against multi-attacker scenarios.

title: Traceable Llm Reasoning For Fake-Order Fraud Detection
authors: Siqi You, Bingsong Xu, Zhixian Zheng, Xinjian Peng, Yang Xie, Ying Wang, Jiarong Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23075v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Detecting fake-order fraud at scale remains a critical challenge for large online-to-offline (O2O) service platforms, as existing approaches often rely on expert-designed features, produce black-box decisions, and provide limited interpretability. To address these limitations, we propose DeepScrub, a reinforcement learning framework built upon large language models (LLMs) for fake-order fraud detection with traceable reasoning. DeepScrub introduces three innovations. First, a semantic unification module converts heterogeneous risk signals into textual descriptions that LLMs can understand. Second, continued pre-training on risk-control corpora injects domain knowledge, and task rewards jointly evaluate prediction correctness and reasoning quality. Third, the SUggest-REflect (SURE) mechanism incorporates expert feedback and model self-checking to iteratively refine reasoning paths. On a real-world fake-order fraud detection dataset, DeepScrub achieves a macro-F1 score of 85.3%, outperforming the best baseline by 2.7 percentage points. Our task-optimized 8B model further surpasses a 32B model, showing that domain adaptation can matter more than model scale in this setting. In a four-week live pilot, DeepScrub achieved 91.8% precision and 88.5% recall, improving over first-stage human reviewers by 16.6 and 38.8 percentage points. It reduced first-stage manual review workload by 94% and saved nearly one million RMB annually. These results show that DeepScrub improves fraud review accuracy, reduces first-stage review workload, and provides traceable evidence for production risk-review workflows.
tldr: This paper applies LLMs with reinforcement learning to detect fake-order fraud in O2O platforms, focusing on traceable reasoning and domain adaptation.
motivation: Existing fraud detection methods rely on expert features and black-box models, lacking interpretability and scalability for large O2O platforms.
method: DeepScrub uses a semantic unification module to convert risk signals to text, continued pre-training on risk corpora, and a SURE mechanism combining expert feedback and self-checking to refine reasoning paths.
result: DeepScrub achieves 85.3% macro-F1 on a real dataset, outperforming baselines by 2.7 points, and in a live pilot reduces manual review workload by 94% while improving precision and recall.
conclusion: Domain-adapted LLMs can effectively detect fake-order fraud with traceable reasoning, reducing human workload and costs.

title: Poster: Rethinking Security In Llm Code Generation Through Real-World Risk Scenarios
authors: Lixun Ma, Ruolong Ma, Bei Wang, Feng Wei, Zhenguang Liu, Lorenzo Cavallaro, Wentao Chen
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are widely used for code generation, yet their security behavior in realistic development workflows remains underexplored. Existing benchmarks often rely on explicitly specified security requirements, failing to capture real-world scenarios where prompts are frequently ambiguous or incomplete. In this paper, we adopt a developer-centric perspective and identify three representative risk scenarios that commonly lead to security vulnerabilities in LLM-generated code: Ambiguous Requirements, Under-Specified Operational Context, and Security--Functionality Conflict. Based on these scenarios, we construct a large-scale benchmark comprising 2,700 test cases, enabling fine-grained evaluation of LLM security under realistic conditions. Extensive evaluation of eight state-of-the-art LLMs reveals that all models exhibit average vulnerability rates exceeding 56\% across risk scenarios. We further demonstrate that security-aware prompting can substantially mitigate these risks, achieving up to 45\% improvement.
tldr: This paper studies security vulnerabilities in LLM-generated code under realistic, ambiguous prompts.
motivation: Existing benchmarks for LLM code security rely on explicit security requirements, ignoring real-world scenarios where prompts are ambiguous or incomplete.
method: The authors identify three risk scenarios (Ambiguous Requirements, Under-Specified Operational Context, Security–Functionality Conflict) and construct a benchmark of 2,700 test cases to evaluate eight state-of-the-art LLMs.
result: All models show average vulnerability rates exceeding 56% across risk scenarios; security-aware prompting can reduce vulnerabilities by up to 45%.
conclusion: LLM-generated code is highly vulnerable in realistic settings, but security-aware prompting can substantially mitigate risks.

title: False Prophets: On The Security Of World Models In Agentic Systems
authors: Erik Imgrund, Anna Wimbauer, Klim Kireev, Konrad Rieck
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models now power autonomous agents capable of complex, multi-step tasks in different environments. Accurate and reliable execution of these tasks requires the agent to predict the results of its actions. Recent research proposes to enhance predictive capabilities via specially trained environment simulators-world models. While world models can improve performance, they can also mislead agents into executing harmful actions, creating significant security and privacy risks. In this paper, we raise security concerns regarding the usage of world models in agentic systems. We discover a range of world model specific vulnerabilities, which can be exploited in terminal-based agents to execute malicious code or extract sensitive data. To facilitate future development, we introduce a security benchmark dataset designed for text-based world models. We argue that some risks are intrinsic to approximate world modeling, and show that attackers can induce mispredictions in agentic pipelines with up to 95% success rate, possibly resulting in unintended command execution, denial of service, drainage of wallet and private information extraction. Finally, we provide practical recommendations for practitioners to mitigate the discovered harms and harden agentic systems.
tldr: This paper studies security vulnerabilities in world models used by LLM-based agents, focusing on adversarial attacks that cause mispredictions leading to harmful actions.
motivation: World models enhance agent performance but can be exploited to mislead agents into executing malicious code or extracting sensitive data, posing security and privacy risks.
method: The authors identify world model-specific vulnerabilities, develop a security benchmark dataset for text-based world models, and demonstrate attacks achieving up to 95% success rate in inducing mispredictions.
result: Attackers can induce mispredictions in agentic pipelines with up to 95% success rate, potentially causing unintended command execution, denial of service, wallet drainage, and private information extraction.
conclusion: Some risks are intrinsic to approximate world modeling; the paper provides practical recommendations to mitigate harms and harden agentic systems.

title: Kairos: Generating Tick-Indexed Proof Obligations For Synchronous Temporal Contracts
authors: Fr\'ed\'eric Dabrowski
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23178v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Requirements for synchronous programs relate observations across ticks, while general-purpose deductive backends use first-order conditions on local steps. Kairos is a prototype toolchain generating such obligations from synchronous programs and source-level temporal safety contracts in assume-guarantee form. Using the standard automata-theoretic reduction, it translates their linear temporal logic (LTL) formulas into bad-state automata, forms their product with the program, and derives tick-indexed Why3 obligations. We formalize the underlying principles and prove reactive contract correctness: under the stated program and automaton hypotheses, every input trace satisfying the environment assumptions induces a unique execution satisfying the temporal guarantees. The definitions, obligation construction, and proof are mechanized in Rocq. A medical infusion controller illustrates the workflow.
tldr: This paper presents Kairos, a toolchain for generating tick-indexed proof obligations from synchronous programs and temporal contracts.
motivation: Synchronous programs require verification of temporal properties across ticks, but general-purpose deductive backends only handle first-order conditions on local steps.
method: Kairos translates LTL formulas into bad-state automata, forms their product with the program, and derives tick-indexed Why3 obligations, with the construction mechanized in Rocq.
result: The paper formalizes the underlying principles and proves reactive contract correctness, demonstrating the workflow on a medical infusion controller.
conclusion: Kairos provides a practical approach to verifying synchronous temporal contracts using deductive verification.

title: Energy-Efficient Dual-Band Communication: How To Allocate Traffic To Sub-THz Carriers?
authors: Anders Enqvist, Emil Bj\"ornson, Cicek Cavdar
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23205v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As 6G wireless networks transition toward sub-Terahertz (sub-THz) frequencies to satisfy extreme capacity demands, managing the trade-off between massive bandwidth and power consumption becomes a critical design challenge. In this paper, we investigate the fundamental energy efficiency (EE) limits of a dual-band base station site combining a coverage-oriented sub-6 GHz carrier with a capacity-oriented sub-THz carrier. By jointly optimizing hardware parameters and advanced sleep modes via activity factors, we identify four distinct operational regions that govern the EE-optimal behavior across the complete range of data rates. We derive closed-form analytical thresholds that dictate precisely when the sub-THz band should awaken from sleep and how to allocate traffic between the bands in that case. Our results demonstrate that utilizing the sub-THz band is EE-optimal when the power cost of the bandwidth-limited sub-6 GHz band surpasses the static power penalty of activating the sub-THz circuitry. Ultimately, this framework provides mathematically rigorous guidelines for power consumption minimization and sleep-mode management in future green networks.
tldr: This paper studies energy-efficient dual-band communication in 6G wireless networks, focusing on sub-THz and sub-6 GHz bands.
motivation: To manage the trade-off between massive bandwidth and power consumption in future 6G networks using sub-THz frequencies.
method: Joint optimization of hardware parameters and sleep modes via activity factors, deriving closed-form analytical thresholds for band activation and traffic allocation.
result: Four operational regions identified; sub-THz band is energy-efficient when the power cost of sub-6 GHz band exceeds the static power penalty of sub-THz circuitry.
conclusion: Provides mathematically rigorous guidelines for power consumption minimization and sleep-mode management in green networks.

title: Movable-Antenna Assisted Energy Minimization In UAV-Enabled Mobile Edge Computing Systems
authors: Jiang Chen, Chunjie Wang, Xuhui Zhang, Yanyan Shen, Kejiang Ye, Chengzhong Xu
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Driven by the exponential growth of latency-sensitive applications, mobile edge computing (MEC) has emerged as a pivotal paradigm, yet mitigating its substantial energy consumption remains critical. This paper explores a movable-antenna (MA) assisted energy minimization scheme in an uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV)-enabled MEC system, where a UAV equipped with an MA array serves as an edge server to process tasks offloaded from terrestrial consumer electronics (CE) devices. To minimize the total system energy consumption, we jointly optimize computation resource allocation, CE transmit power, receive beamforming, and MA positions. To tackle the resulting non-convex problem with coupled variables, a robust alternating optimization algorithm based on the block coordinate descent method is developed. The problem is iteratively decomposed into three subproblems. In particular, the subproblem of transmit power and receive beamforming is reformulated and optimized using the quadratic transform technique, while the MA array positions are optimized via the particle swarm optimization algorithm. Numerical simulations verify that the proposed scheme achieves substantial energy savings over conventional benchmarks.
tldr: This paper proposes a movable-antenna assisted energy minimization scheme in UAV-enabled mobile edge computing systems.
motivation: The exponential growth of latency-sensitive applications demands efficient mobile edge computing, but energy consumption remains a critical challenge.
method: A robust alternating optimization algorithm based on block coordinate descent is developed, jointly optimizing computation resource allocation, transmit power, receive beamforming, and MA positions.
result: Numerical simulations show substantial energy savings compared to conventional benchmarks.
conclusion: The proposed MA-assisted scheme effectively reduces energy consumption in UAV-enabled MEC systems.

title: Int8 Quantization Makes Arm Edge Inference Dispatch-Invariant
authors: Shenied E. Maldonado Guerra Sebasti\'an A. Cruz Romero
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On x86, kernel dispatch fragments the outputs of the same neural network into many equivalence classes across hardware. We ask whether the same fragmentation governs ARM edge inference, where most edge ML actually runs. Across four Raspberry Pi devices spanning Cortex-A53, A72, and A76 under ONNX Runtime CPU, microarchitecture is not observable in the outputs of a fixed FP32 CNN. Holding hardware constant at Cortex-A76 and switching only the execution provider, FP32 outputs disagree on every CIFAR-10 image with a mean remaining precision of 14.97 of 23 mantissa bits. INT8 QDQ post-training quantization collapses both axes to a single equivalence class. We trace this to a structural property of QDQ graphs that we call H1+H2: discrete-grid inputs make any Conv dispatch-deterministic (H1) and QuantizeLinear at every layer boundary preserves that precondition (H2). H1+H2 predicts that bit-exact agreement should extend to production CNNs under runtimes that confirmably exercise different ARM microkernels. We verify this on MobileNetV2 and ResNet50V2 under TensorFlow Lite with XNNPACK, where timing evidence confirms SDOT dispatch on A76 and NEON multiply-accumulate on A72 yet every intermediate INT32 accumulator and every final output is byte-identical across 500 ImageNet images per model. We then identify the specific x86 mechanism that breaks the same invariant on x86, namely PMADDUBSW saturating INT16 intermediates, which has no ARM analogue. The Schl\"ogl et al. divergence phenomenon is delineated rather than contradicted. For practitioners deploying quantized CNNs across heterogeneous ARM fleets, the operational consequence is direct. INT8 inference is the reproducible mode and the relevant behavioral variation axis is precision, not microarchitecture.
tldr: This paper studies the reproducibility of quantized neural network inference on ARM edge devices, showing that INT8 quantization eliminates hardware-dependent output variation.
motivation: On x86, neural network inference outputs vary across hardware due to kernel dispatch, and the authors investigate whether similar fragmentation occurs on ARM edge devices where most edge ML runs.
method: The authors compare FP32 and INT8 quantized inference across multiple Raspberry Pi devices and execution providers, analyzing output agreement and tracing the cause to structural properties of QDQ graphs (H1+H2).
result: FP32 outputs disagree across devices and providers, but INT8 quantization collapses all variation into a single equivalence class, with byte-identical outputs across different ARM microarchitectures.
conclusion: INT8 inference is the reproducible mode for ARM edge inference, and practitioners should focus on precision rather than microarchitecture as the relevant variation axis.

title: Network Allocation Games With Anonymous Preferences
authors: Argyrios Deligkas, Eduard Eiben, \v{s}imon Schierreich, Alexandros A. Voudouris
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study network allocation games in which a set of agents must be allocated to (a subset of) the vertices of a graph topology. The agents are anonymous and strategic: Each of them aims to maximize her utility, which is a function of the number of agents in the neighborhood of their allocated vertex. We focus on the existence and the computation of stable allocations under various notions of stability. More specifically, we study swap-based stability notions, where agents can exchange locations between them, and jump-based stability notions, where agents can jump to an empty vertex of the graph. For almost all stability notions we consider, we provide dichotomies between existence and intractability that depend on the structure of the utility functions of the agents and the topology. In addition, we prove strong intractability results for computing welfare-maximizing allocations and for verifying whether a given allocation is Pareto optimal.
tldr: This paper studies network allocation games with anonymous agents and various stability notions, focusing on existence and computation of stable allocations.
motivation: To understand how strategic agents can be allocated to vertices of a graph when they only care about the number of agents in their neighborhood, and to characterize when stable allocations exist.
method: The authors model the problem as a game with anonymous preferences, define swap-based and jump-based stability notions, and analyze existence and computational complexity using combinatorial arguments and reductions from NP-hard problems.
result: They provide dichotomies between existence and intractability depending on utility function structure and graph topology, and prove strong intractability for welfare-maximizing allocations and Pareto optimality verification.
conclusion: The existence of stable allocations is highly sensitive to the stability notion and utility structure, and computing optimal allocations is generally hard.

title: Exploiting Movable Antennas For Multi-Target Wireless Sensing System In Multipath Environments
authors: Xiang Chen, Ming-Min Zhao, Lebin Chen, Jie Xu, Min-Jian Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the multi-target detection problem in a movable-antenna (MA)-enabled wireless sensing system with linear arrays, in which both the direct line-of-sight (LoS) paths and the first-order non-LoS (NLoS) paths are explicitly considered. Unlike conventional fixed-position antenna arrays, MAs provide additional design degrees of freedom by enabling adaptive antenna positioning to reconfigure the propagation geometry, offering great potential to enhance the sensing performance in complex multi-target multipath scenarios. Under this setup, we first develop a cross sparsity Markov mixture prior to derive the posterior probabilities of target locations, in which the structural correlation between the LoS and NLoS paths is effectively exploited to enhance the location estimation accuracy. Based on the derived posterior probabilities, we further analyze the angular-domain sensing performance for multi-target detection by proposing a new two-dimensional (2D) ambiguity function as the performance metric. Next, we optimize the MA positions to suppress the sidelobe levels and narrow the mainlobe width of the proposed ambiguity function. Although the resulting problem is highly non-convex, we develop a low-complexity Dykstra-based projected gradient descent algorithm to solve it efficiently. Finally, simulation results verify the accuracy of the proposed ambiguity function analysis, demonstrate the substantial performance gains enabled by the proposed prior model and MAs, and show that the proposed algorithm achieves performance comparable to existing methods with significantly lower computational complexity.
tldr: This paper proposes a movable-antenna-enabled wireless sensing system for multi-target detection in multipath environments, focusing on antenna position optimization to enhance sensing performance.
motivation: Conventional fixed-position antenna arrays have limited flexibility in complex multipath scenarios; movable antennas can adaptively reconfigure propagation geometry to improve sensing accuracy.
method: A cross sparsity Markov mixture prior is developed to derive posterior probabilities of target locations, and a 2D ambiguity function is proposed as a performance metric. Antenna positions are optimized via a low-complexity Dykstra-based projected gradient descent algorithm.
result: Simulations verify the accuracy of the ambiguity function analysis and demonstrate substantial performance gains from the proposed prior model and movable antennas, with lower computational complexity compared to existing methods.
conclusion: Movable antennas offer significant potential for enhancing multi-target wireless sensing in multipath environments, and the proposed optimization algorithm efficiently achieves near-optimal performance.

title: From Signals To Behaviors: Evidence-Based Android Malware Detection
authors: Shiwen Song, Yiheng Xiong, Sen Chen, Xiaofei Xie
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23272v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Android malware remains a persistent threat, and detecting it accurately is a long-standing open problem. Whether an app is malicious depends on what it actually does and the context in which it does it, not on the surface signals it happens to exhibit. Existing detectors instead reason about proxies for behavior, such as learned features or local code slices, and flag whatever deviates from these proxies as malicious. But deviation is not maliciousness: benign apps that merely look unusual are over-flagged, evolving malware that looks ordinary slips through. We argue that detection should be behavior-oriented: recover an app's potentially malicious behaviors and judge which are truly malicious. To realize this, we present Praxis, which structures detection as a hypothesize-confirm-judge pipeline: it hypothesizes candidate behaviors from coarse static signals, confirms each by grounding it in code evidence verified with program analysis, and judges the confirmed behaviors in context: the user's awareness, the app's functional context, and how they compose into an attack. For a malicious app, Praxis returns a verdict and the supported behaviors. We evaluate Praxis against seven baselines across three challenging settings. It achieves the best overall detection performance (87.4% F1), outperforming the baselines by 18.6-34.8 percentage points. On high-permission benign apps, it reduces the false-positive rate to 13.0%, a reduction of 41.1-67.0 percentage points compared with the baselines. Beyond binary detection, Praxis recovers fine-grained malicious behaviors at 87.3% F1, outperforming prior behavior-level approaches by 56.5-73.4 percentage points. Ablation studies show that each stage of the pipeline contributes to the final performance.
tldr: This paper presents a behavior-oriented Android malware detection method called Praxis.
motivation: Existing malware detectors rely on surface signals and proxies for behavior, leading to high false positives and inability to detect evolving malware.
method: Praxis uses a hypothesize-confirm-judge pipeline: it hypothesizes candidate behaviors from static signals, confirms them with program analysis, and judges them in context.
result: Praxis achieves 87.4% F1 in detection, outperforming baselines by 18.6-34.8 percentage points, and recovers fine-grained malicious behaviors at 87.3% F1.
conclusion: Behavior-oriented detection is effective for Android malware, significantly reducing false positives and improving detection of novel malware.

title: Hiding In Plain Sight: An Effective Physical Adversarial Patch Attack Against Visual-Infrared Fused Face Detection
authors: Qiucheng Yu, Tao Ni, Yihe Zhou, Jiayimei Wang, Qingchuan Zhao
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep learning-based visual-infrared fused face detection models are increasingly deployed across a wide range of applications, yet they remain susceptible to adversarial patch attacks. Most prior attacks target either the visual or the infrared image alone in the digital domain, which renders them ineffective against fused models in the physical world. Moreover, many of these methods are readily noticeable, as their patch patterns deviate substantially from those seen in the real world. In this paper, we introduce VIPatch (Visual-Infrared Patch), a novel physical adversarial patch attack that produces inconspicuous, realistic, and natural-looking patches for facial images. Specifically, VIPatch crafts a gradient-color mask together with a band-aid sticker across both the visual and infrared images, and jointly optimizes these two elements; the resulting digital patches further guide the fabrication of their physical counterparts. Experimental results show that VIPatch achieves competitive attack success rates (over 90%) in both the digital and physical domains, while keeping the patches unobtrusive to human observers.
tldr: This paper presents a physical adversarial patch attack against visual-infrared fused face detection models.
motivation: Deep learning-based fused face detection models are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, but existing attacks are either limited to single modalities or easily noticeable.
method: VIPatch crafts a gradient-color mask and a band-aid sticker jointly optimized across visual and infrared images, then fabricates physical patches.
result: VIPatch achieves over 90% attack success rate in both digital and physical domains while remaining unobtrusive.
conclusion: The proposed method demonstrates effective and inconspicuous physical adversarial attacks on fused face detection systems.

title: Online Fair Division With Budget Constraints
authors: Saar Cohen, Nicholas Teh, Paul W. Goldberg, Michael J. Wooldridge
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23310v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an online variant of discrete fair division under generalized assignment budget constraints. Goods arrive one at a time and must be assigned irrevocably to a feasible agent or to charity, which holds all unallocated goods, while fairness is evaluated only against budget-feasible subsets of every recipient's bundle. We first show that, without additional structure, no deterministic online algorithm can guarantee any fixed approximation to feasible envy-freeness, even in highly symmetric instances. We then identify bounded density spread as a structural condition that restores meaningful guarantees, obtaining approximation algorithms for arbitrary item sizes and showing that, under common valuations and sufficiently small goods, these guarantees can be strengthened to an optimal deterministic frontier. We further study resource augmentation, where the online algorithm is allowed slightly larger budgets than the fairness benchmark, and characterize the resulting improvement in the achievable guarantees. Finally, we develop a learning-augmented framework based on predicting joint value-size types, proving consistency under perfect predictions, robustness to prediction error, and showing that separate predictions of value and size marginals are insufficient to recover strong fairness guarantees.
tldr: This paper studies online fair division with budget constraints, a topic in algorithmic game theory and economics, with no connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: The paper addresses the problem of allocating goods online under budget constraints while ensuring fairness, which is a classic problem in economics and computer science.
method: The authors analyze deterministic online algorithms, identify bounded density spread as a structural condition, and develop a learning-augmented framework using predictions of joint value-size types.
result: They show that without additional structure no deterministic algorithm can guarantee envy-freeness, but under bounded density spread approximation algorithms exist; resource augmentation and learning-augmented approaches improve guarantees.
conclusion: The work provides theoretical foundations for online fair division with budgets, but is unrelated to the user's research interests in quantum information theory and information thermodynamics.

title: A Structured Cyber Threat Intelligence Dataset Using Stix 2.1 Entities And Mitre Att&ck Mappings
authors: Dipshikha Das, Arnab Banik, Md. Shariful Islam, Md Rayhanur Rahman
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Cyber threat intelligence (CTI) reports are typically written in unstructured formats, which complicates the extraction and analysis of important entities and adversarial behaviors. Although existing CTI research provides extraction tools, knowledge-graph frameworks, and MITRE ATT&CK mapped datasets, curated report-level datasets that preserve complex entity relationships and normalized adversarial behaviors remain limited. To address this limitation, this study presents a manually constructed dataset of 150 English-language CTI reports, each represented as STIX 2.1 based graphs, which includes 4,777 STIX entities, 5,817 STIX relationships in total, and 1,273 STIX attack-pattern entities (adversarial behaviors) mapped to 269 unique MITRE ATT&CK Enterprise techniques and sub-techniques. Twenty five randomly sampled reports were independently assessed by two cybersecurity researchers, which shows substantial inter-rater agreement. Disagreements were subsequently adjudicated to establish a gold-standard reference dataset. Four locally deployed open-source LLMs were evaluated as automated judges against this adjudicated reference sample. Qwen3.6:27B achieved the strongest overall performance, with a maximum kappa score of 0.803, micro-F1 scores exceeding 92%, and false-positive rates below 5%. The dataset provides a benchmark for CTI information extraction, knowledge-graph construction, incident analysis, and threat attribution. The findings further indicate that locally deployed LLMs can support human reviewers in identifying annotation inconsistencies, but expert validation remains essential.
tldr: This paper presents a manually curated dataset of cyber threat intelligence reports annotated with STIX 2.1 entities and MITRE ATT&CK mappings, and evaluates LLMs as automated judges.
motivation: CTI reports are unstructured, making extraction and analysis difficult; existing datasets lack complex entity relationships and normalized adversarial behaviors.
method: 150 CTI reports were manually annotated as STIX 2.1 graphs, including 4,777 entities and 5,817 relationships, with 1,273 attack patterns mapped to MITRE ATT&CK. Two researchers independently assessed 25 reports, and four open-source LLMs were evaluated as automated judges.
result: Qwen3.6:27B achieved the best performance with a kappa of 0.803, micro-F1 >92%, and false-positive rate <5%.
conclusion: The dataset provides a benchmark for CTI extraction and analysis; locally deployed LLMs can assist but expert validation remains essential.

title: Exploring The Ooda Loop As A Systematic Way Of Thinking In Coping With Conflicts
authors: Shouhuai Xu Ethan Anderson
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When conflicts emerge, we need systematic ways of thinking to deal with them. This paper revisits Boyd's Observe, Orient, Decide, Act (OODA) loop and explores its usefulness as a systematic way of thinking for reasoning about conflicts in dynamic environments characterized by uncertainty, adaptation, and adversarial interference. We explore the OODA loop beyond its origin in air warfare where it focuses attention on the relationship between information, understanding, choice, and action. Our exploration is conducted in two application domains: cyber conflicts and cognitive conflicts. Across both domains, we emphasize situational awareness as a critical mechanism of orientation, while noting that observations become useful only when they are perceived, comprehended, projected into possible futures, and integrated with mental models, objectives, doctrine, trust, and experience. Our exploration suggests that conflict is not merely a contest of actions or effects, but a contest over the ability to generate, protect, and leverage one's own superior observation, orientation, and decision, while degrading and exploiting adversary's observation, orientation, and decision.
tldr: This paper explores the OODA loop as a systematic thinking framework for coping with conflicts in dynamic environments, applied to cyber and cognitive domains.
motivation: Conflicts in dynamic environments require systematic reasoning; the OODA loop offers a model for information, understanding, choice, and action.
method: Conceptual analysis and application of Boyd's OODA loop to cyber conflicts and cognitive conflicts, emphasizing situational awareness.
result: The OODA loop provides a useful framework for reasoning about conflicts, highlighting the contest over observation, orientation, and decision capabilities.
conclusion: Conflict is not just about actions but about generating and protecting superior OODA processes while degrading the adversary's.

title: Fair Division With Strictly Increasing Valuations: A Tight Threshold For Two-Agent Ef1 And Po
authors: Nicholas Teh
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23367v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study whether strictly positive marginal values restore the compatibility of envy-freeness up to one good (EF1) and Pareto optimality (PO) for indivisible goods. For two agents, we identify the exact threshold in the number of goods. Every instance with at most seven goods and strictly increasing valuations admits an allocation that is both EF1 and PO, without any submodularity assumption. In contrast, we construct an eight-good instance with normalized, integer-valued, strictly increasing, submodular valuations in which every EF1 allocation is strictly Pareto dominated. Thus, eight goods are necessary and sufficient for a two-agent counterexample. Finally, we strengthen the three-agent NP-hardness result of Chandramouleeswaran and Nimbhorkar (2026): deciding whether an EF1 and PO allocation exists remains NP-hard for normalized, integer-valued, monotone submodular valuations even when zero marginals are confined to eight fixed agent-good pairs, all involving a single agent.
tldr: This paper studies fair division of indivisible goods with strictly increasing valuations, identifying a tight threshold for EF1 and PO allocations for two agents.
motivation: To determine whether strictly positive marginal values restore compatibility of EF1 and PO for indivisible goods, and to find the exact number of goods needed for a counterexample.
method: The paper uses combinatorial constructions and complexity analysis to prove existence and non-existence of EF1+PO allocations for two agents, and strengthens NP-hardness results for three agents.
result: For two agents, every instance with at most seven goods and strictly increasing valuations admits an EF1+PO allocation, but an eight-good counterexample exists. For three agents, NP-hardness holds even with restricted zero marginals.
conclusion: Strictly increasing valuations do not guarantee EF1+PO compatibility beyond a small number of goods, and the problem remains computationally hard for three agents.

title: Rendering On Real Silicon: Gpu Render-Timing As A Passive, AI-Resistant Captcha Signal
authors: Forrest Mckee David Noever
abstract: ArXiv:2607.23389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Conventional CAPTCHAs pose puzzles that modern AI systems increasingly solve, while behavioral and cryptographic-attestation defenses carry privacy or enrollment costs. We investigate an orthogonal signal: the physical timing behavior of a client's GPU under a controlled WebGL rendering workload. Unlike WebGL fingerprinting, which hashes pixel output into a static device identifier, we measure render-timing dynamics to classify rather than identify, leaking no persistent identifier.
